units.tr: DE BABYLO

units.la: ἀχίων ἄιρίθῃ ἐ πολλῶν ἡ ἰσφαγμένων ὅτι ἡ γῆς.
units.tr: ...of many who were slain upon the earth [πάντων τῶν ἐσφαγμένων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς].

units.la: Capu A versu. 1. a
units.tr: Chapter 19, verse 1.

units.la: 1. Καὶ μὴ ταῦτα ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴ ὄχλε πολὺ μεγάλων ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, λέγοντος· Ἀλληλουϊα· ἡ σωτηρία, ἡ δόξα, ἡ τιμὴ, ἡ δύναμις Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν.
units.tr: After these things I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying: Alleluia; salvation, glory, honour and power to the Lord our God [Μετὰ ταῦτα ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ὄχλου πολλοῦ μεγάλην ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λεγόντων· Ἀλληλουϊα· ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δύναμις τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν].

units.la: 2. Ὅτι ἀληθιναὶ ἡ δικαιῶσαι αἱ κρίσεις αὐτοῦ· ὅτι ἔκρινε τὴν πόρνην τὴν μεγάλην, ἥτις ἔφθειρε τὴν γῆν ἐν τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐξεδίκησε τὸ αἷμα τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ ἐκ χειρὸς αὐτῆς.
units.tr: For true and righteous are his judgments; for he has judged the great harlot, who corrupted the earth with her fornication, and has avenged the blood of his servants at her hand [Ὅτι ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις αὐτοῦ· ὅτι ἔκρινε τὴν πόρνην τὴν μεγάλην, ἥτις ἔφθειρε τὴν γῆν ἐν τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐξεδίκησε τὸ αἷμα τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ ἐκ χειρὸς αὐτῆς].

units.la: 3. Καὶ δεύτερον εἰρήκαμεν· Ἀλληλουϊα· Καὶ ὁ καπνὸς αὐτῆς ἀναβαίνει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
units.tr: And a second time they said: Alleluia. And her smoke rises up for ever and ever [Καὶ δεύτερον εἰρήκασι· Ἀλληλουϊα. Καὶ ὁ καπνὸς αὐτῆς ἀναβαίνει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων].

units.la: 4. Καὶ ἔπεσον οἱ πρεσβύτεροι οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες, καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ Θεῷ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ, λέγοντες· Ἀμὴν, Ἀλληλουϊα.
units.tr: And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshipped God who sits on the throne, saying: Amen, Alleluia [Καὶ ἔπεσαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ Θεῷ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ, λέγοντες· Ἀμήν, Ἀλληλουϊα].

units.la: 5. Καὶ φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου ἐξῆλθε, λέγουσα· Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν πάντες οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ, καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι αὐτὸν, οἱ μικροὶ καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι.
units.tr: And a voice came out from the throne, saying: Praise our God, all you his servants, and you who fear him, both small and great [Καὶ φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου ἐξῆλθε λέγουσα· Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν, πάντες οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ, καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι αὐτόν, οἱ μικροὶ καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι].

units.la: 6. Καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ὄχλου πολλῶν, καὶ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν, καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῶν ἰσχυρῶν, λεγόντων· Ἀλληλουϊα· ὅτι ἐβασίλευσε Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ.
units.tr: And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunders, saying: Alleluia, for the Lord God Almighty reigns [Καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ὄχλου πολλοῦ, καὶ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν, καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῶν ἰσχυρῶν, λεγόντων· Ἀλληλουϊα, ὅτι ἐβασίλευσε Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ].

units.la: 7. Χαίρωμεν καὶ ἀγαλλιώμεθα, καὶ δώσωμεν sanctorum inventus est, & omnium mactatorum in terra.
units.tr: Let us rejoice and be glad, and let us give glory to him, and the blood of the saints was found in it, and of all who have been slain upon the earth. [Χαίρωμεν καὶ ἀγαλλιώμεθα, καὶ δώσωμεν (αὐτῷ τὴν δόξαν)].

units.la: T XIX.
units.tr: Chapter XIX.

units.la: ad versum. 11.
units.tr: On verse 11.

units.la: 1. Et post hac audivi tanquam vocem turbæ multæ magnam in cælo, dicentis : Alleluja : Salus & gloria & honor & potentia Domino Deo nostro.
units.tr: 1. And after these things I heard, as it were, the voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying: Alleluia: Salvation and glory and honour and power to the Lord our God.

units.la: 2. Quia vera & justa sunt judicia ejus : quia judicavit meretricem magnam, quæ corrupit terram fornicatione sua, & vindicavit sanguinem servorum suorum ex manu ejus.
units.tr: 2. For true and just are his judgments: for he has judged the great harlot, who corrupted the earth with her fornication, and has avenged the blood of his servants at her hand.

units.la: 3. (Et secundò dixerunt : Alleluja) Et fumus ejus ascendit in sæcula sæculorum.
units.tr: 3. (And a second time they said: Alleluia.) And her smoke rose up for ever and ever.

units.la: 4. Et ceciderunt Seniores viginti quatuor & quatuor animalia, & adoravérunt Deum qui sedebat in throno, dicentes : Amen, Alleluja.
units.tr: 4. And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshipped God who sat on the throne, saying: Amen, Alleluia.

units.la: 5. Et vox ex throno exivit, dicens: Laudate Deum vestrum omnes servi ejus, & , qui timetis eum, & parvi & magni.
units.tr: 5. And a voice came out from the throne, saying: Praise our God, all you his servants, and you who fear him, both small and great.

units.la: 6. Et audivi tanquam vocem turbæ multæ , & ut vocem aquarum multarum, & ut vocem tonitruum validorum, dicentium : Alleluja. Quia regnum capessivit Dominus Deus omnipotens.
units.tr: 6. And I heard, as it were, the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunders, saying: Alleluia. For the Lord God Almighty has taken up his reign.

units.la: 7. Lætemur & exultemus & demus glo-
units.tr: 7. Let us rejoice and exult and give glory

units.la: VATICINIUM DE P
units.tr: PROPHECY CONCERNING P

units.la: μὴν ⸗ δόξαν αὐτῆ· ὅτι ἦλθεν ὁ χάμ ... ⸗ ἡ ... ἐχει ... ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ ἡτοίμασεν ἑαυτὴν.
units.tr: ...let us rejoice and be glad and give glory to him, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready. [μὴν ... δόξαν αὐτῆ· ὅτι ἦλθεν ὁ γάμος ... ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ ἡτοίμασεν ἑαυτήν]

units.la: 8. Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῇ, ἵνα περιβάληται βύσσινον καθαρὸν καὶ λαμπρὸν· τὸ γὰρ βύσσινον τὰ δικαιώματα τῶν ἁγίων.
units.tr: 8. And it was granted to her that she should be clothed in fine linen, clean and bright: for the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints. [Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῇ, ἵνα περιβάληται βύσσινον καθαρὸν καὶ λαμπρόν· τὸ γὰρ βύσσινον τὰ δικαιώματα τῶν ἁγίων.]

units.la: 9. Καὶ λέγει μοι· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τοῦ γάμου τοῦ ἀρνίου κεκλημένοι. Καὶ λέγει μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι ἀληθινοὶ εἰσι τοῦ Θεοῦ.
units.tr: 9. And he says to me: Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he says to me: These are the true sayings of God. [Καὶ λέγει μοι· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τοῦ γάμου τοῦ ἀρνίου κεκλημένοι. Καὶ λέγει μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι ἀληθινοί εἰσι τοῦ Θεοῦ.]

units.la: 10. Καὶ ἔπεσον ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ προσκυνῆσαι αὐτῷ· καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. τῷ Θεῷ προσκύνησον. ἡ γὰρ μαρτυρία τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐστιν τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς προφητείας. gloriam ipsi : quia venerunt nuptiæ agni & uxor ejus se præparavit.
units.tr: 10. And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he says to me: See that you do not do so; I am your fellow servant and of your brethren who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy. [Καὶ ἔπεσον ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ προσκυνῆσαι αὐτῷ· καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. τῷ Θεῷ προσκύνησον. ἡ γὰρ μαρτυρία τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐστιν τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς προφητείας.] Give glory to him, for the marriage of the Lamb has come and his wife has made herself ready.

units.la: 8. Et datum est ei, ut amiciret se bysso pura & splendida. Nam byssus sunt argumenta justitiæ sanctorum.
units.tr: 8. And it was granted to her that she should clothe herself in pure and bright fine linen. For the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints.

units.la: 9. Et dicit mihi: scribe, Beati, qui ad cœnam nuptiarum agni vocati sunt. Et dicit mihi : Hi sermones veri sunt Dei.
units.tr: 9. And he says to me: Write, Blessed are they who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he says to me: These are the true words of God.

units.la: 10. Et cecidi coram pedibus ejus, ut adorarem eum: & dicit mihi: Vide ne FECERIS. Conservus tuus sum & fratrum tuorum, qui habent testimonium JESU. Deum adora. Nam testimonium JESU est Spiritus prophetiæ.
units.tr: 10. And I fell at his feet to worship him, and he says to me: See that you do not do it. I am your fellow servant and that of your brethren who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.

units.la: SERENISSIMI ET POTENTISSIMI PRINCIPIS JACOBI PRIMI, Magnæ Britanniæ, Scotiæ & Hy- berniæ Regis, In Vaticinium S. Johannis Theologi, DE BABYLONE MAGNA, PARAPHRASIS.
units.tr: Paraphrase of the Prophecy of St John the Divine concerning Great Babylon, dedicated to the Most Serene and Most Mighty Prince James the First, King of Great Britain, Scotland and Ireland.

units.la: CAPUT XVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVII.

units.la: Angelus Joanni manifestam facit, & perspicuam hanc Papæ visionem: fuséque illum describit: tum auctores modumque exitii illius clarissimè explicat.
units.tr: The angel makes this vision of the Pope plain and clear to John, describes it at length, and sets out most clearly its authors and the manner of its destruction.

units.la: 2. At quoniam non satis capiebam, quid sibi vellent hæ plagæ; quid item Babylon, quæ illis percussa dicebatur; eapropter unus ex Angelis, qui Phialas effuderant, mihi dixit, Heus tu, ego tibi familiarius exponam magnæ illius meretricis damnationem, tum verò quænam illa sit, quæ super multas aquas sedeat; 2. Cum qua Spiritualem stupri consuetudinem habuerunt Reges, & cujus fortationis vino inebriati sunt terræ incolæ; nempe ingens variarum gentium colluvies, ad quas nihil attinet electionis mysterium: ut suprà fuit indicatum: 3. tum me per Spiritum (ut in ipso hujus epistolæ limine vobis significavi) abripuit Angelus in desertum, quo nomine Gentilitas significatur, Esaia teste. Nam Bestia cum suis omnibus, reapse gentiles sunt, ut in sexta audiveris tuba: & juxta Domini nostri pronuntiatum, quisquis nobiscum non colligit, spargit: nec enim magis invenitur medium inter duos hosce athlothetas, Deum & Diabolum; quàm inter eorum præmia, cælum & infernum: & quemadmodum fieri non potest, quin alterum è duobus illis Dominis sequamur in vita; ita pariter necesse est ad alterum è duobus illis locis, post hanc vitam, proficiscamur. Tum vidi in cremo mulierem ipsam, nimirum Babylonem; meretricem illam, insidentem coccinæ & sanguinolentæ bestiæ, sicut ame humana specie insidebat equo pallido, in quarto sigillo. Et hæc bestia blasphemiæ plena erat, & septem capita habebat, & decem cornua, ut supra. 4. erat autem mulier illa amicta purpurâ, & cocco, & gemmis, & margaritis: manu autem aureum poculum tenebat. Monarchia enim hæc, & ejus Monarcha, etiam corporali hujusmodi colorum magnificentia vestientur; gemmis, & margaritis splendentes. Porrò colores hi, omnium maximè illustres, & hæc decora gemmarum indicant nihil fore hac Monarchia, ejusque sede gloriosius; aut in mundi conspectu (ut supra monui) splendidius: nec tamen pomposa hac honoris specie veram Dei referet Ecclesiam; verùm etiam è communibus syncerè religionis principiis multa retinebit, quod aureo poculo significatur. Veruntamen illud ipsum poculum plenum erat abominationibus, & immunditiâ Spiritualis fornicationis ejus: nam quinquâm in multis veritatem retinet, quâ, tanquam illecebrâ, credulis insidietur, eòsque in amorem sui pelliciat; eam tamen pestifero suarum hæresèon, & traditionum veneno, & Spiritualis sui adulterii impuritate inficiet: ut dictum est prius. 5. Et fronti ejus mysterium inscriptum erat: Babylon illa magna: nempe Spiritualis illa Babylon (ut supra) mater fornicationum & abominationum terræ: quæ etenim hæresès & corruptelæ omnium maximæ sunt, & solæ ferè præcipuæ dici merentur, ex ea nascentur, & illæ quidem speciosò Christianitatis titulo relatæ: hisce præter cæteros inquinabuntur, usque ad consummationem sæculi, quibus vox hæc in labiis natat, Domine, Domine: neque tantùm Babylon hosce errores, ut mater, pariet; verùm etiam, ut nutrix, eos fovebit, alet, proteget. Mysterium autem hoc dicitur, quia licet in publico & propatulo omnium oculis expositum sit, (quod frontis inscriptione indicatur) iis tamen solis nequitiam hanc dabitur intueri, à quorum oculis divinæ misericordiæ ope glaucoma remota est. 6. Et vidi mulierem illam ebriam sanguine Sanctorum, & martyrum Jesu Salvatoris. Sitiet enim absque modo, & ratione, & miseratione; atque avidissimè hauriet sanguinem Sanctorum, ut sæpe audivistis prius: & cùm viderem eam, valde eam miratus sum: neque enim intellectu penetrare poteram in septem capita, & decem cornua bestiæ, cui insidebat. 7. Ergo Angelus qui eam mihi monstraverat (ut antè percepistis) quum me animadverteret admiratione perculsum: noli (inquit) mirari: ego tibi revelabo mysterium mulieris & bestiæ, quæ eam portat, quæ habet capita septem & cornua decem: 8. hæc bestia, quam vidisti, vel Monarchia per eam significata (quarta enim innuitur Monarchia, illa valivalidissima omnium & quondam florentissima} fuit, & non est : adeò nunc videlicet diminutâ ptiore potentiâ, ut quodammodo dici possit non esse : de novo autem, ut primum vulnus capitis persanatum erit, ex abysso emersura est : nec tamen effugiet imminentem ruinam : incolæ autem terræ, quorum nomina in libro vitæ ante jacta mundi fundamenta scripta non sunt, rapientur in admirationem, quæ omnia antehac percepistis : mirabuntur, inquam, bestiam quæ fuit, (nimirum florida & potens) & jam non est (quadantenus videlicet, ut modò percepistis) & adhuc est (nimirum suis etiamnum nixa fundamentis, licet multò quàm antehac debilior.) 9. Arrigite aures ad ea, quæ vobis aperio : hic enim tanquam ad lydium lapidem explorabitur hominum sapientia ; ut ex meis verbis intelligant, quæ tandem Monarchia, quæ tyrannis hic describitur. Septem bestiæ capitibus tum septem montes significantur, super quibus fundata est augusta hujus Imperii sedes : tum septem Reges ; vel totidem Magistratuum genera, quibus hæc Monarchia antehac usa est, & posthac utetur : 10. quinque eorum fuêre ; unus nunc est, nimirum sextus ; alius sequetur, nempe septimus ; sed necdum venit ; & quum venerit, exiguo sanè tempore manebit. 11. Bestia autem hæc, quæ erat (nempe adeò potens) & non est (ut modò audivistis, nam jam decrescit) est octavus ille, & tamen unus è septem. Etenim hæc bestia è ruderibus quartæ Monarchiæ excitata (ut jam explicatum est) quum in hominum conscientias hæreticam usurpatura sit tyrannidem, propter hoc novum genus politiæ distinguitur à cæteris : & hanc ob causam dicitur octavus ille : nihilominus, quia eandem imperii sedem cum cæteris sortitur, & pari & majore superbia orbi terrarum dominabitur, eâdem denique civilis politiæ formâ, cum uno, quóque è septem illis, utetur, propter hanc, inquam, tam multiplicem similitudinem, septem illis hanc quóque bestiam adnumero. 12. Decem autem cornua, quæ vidisti, decem Reges significant ; numerosos, nimirum, illos in singulis provinciis Magistratus, huic quartæ Monarchiæ subordinatos, qui regnum suum nondum acceperunt : nam sub omnibus illis Politiæ speciebus, quibus Imperium illud variabitur, præterquam sub ultima hac & hæretica ; Magistratus inferiores & subordinati in subditorum numero futuri sunt : at cum Bestia regalem accipient potestatem : nimirum quo tempore Apollyon ille è quarta bestiæ cineribus suscitabitur ; è ruinis, inquam, quartæ Monarchiæ ; continuò Reges terræ, se se illi in servitutem addicent, tanquam Magistratus illi subordinati ; quum tamen ante id tempus, illius Monarchiæ robur in solis imperii subditis fuerit : atque ita cornua, vel vires illius bestiæ, ante vulnus illud acceptum, è meris subditis constabant : at, eo vulnere persanato, Reges hujus mundi & Imperatores in cornua illius & robur degencrabunt. 13. Hi unius erunt sententiæ : & vires & auctoritatem suam bestiæ tradent : nempe ultrò
units.tr: 2. But since I did not sufficiently grasp what these plagues meant, nor what Babylon, which was said to be struck by them, was, one of the angels who had poured out the vials said to me, Look, I will explain to you more familiarly the condemnation of that great harlot, and who she is who sits upon many waters; 2. with whom the kings had a spiritual habit of fornication, and by whose wine of fornication the inhabitants of the earth were made drunk; namely, a vast jumble of various nations, to whom the mystery of election has no bearing, as was indicated above; 3. then the angel carried me away in the Spirit (as I signalled to you at the very threshold of this letter) into the desert, a name by which Gentility is signified, as Isaiah bears witness. For the Beast with all its followers is in fact gentile, as you heard at the sixth trumpet; and according to the saying of our Lord, he who does not gather with us, scatters. For no middle ground is found between these two contestants, God and the Devil, any more than between their rewards, heaven and hell; and just as we cannot help following one of those two lords in life, so likewise we must set out, after this life, for one of those two places. Then I saw in the wilderness the woman herself, namely Babylon, that harlot sitting upon a scarlet and bloody beast, just as the one with a human face sat upon the pale horse at the fourth seal. And this beast was full of blasphemy, and had seven heads and ten horns, as above. 4. The woman was clothed in purple, scarlet, gems and pearls, and in her hand she held a golden cup. For this monarchy and its monarch are likewise clothed in such bodily magnificence of colours, glittering with gems and pearls. Moreover, these colours, the most illustrious of all, and these ornaments of gems, indicate that nothing will be more glorious than this monarchy and its seat, or more splendid in the eyes of the world (as I warned above); yet this pompous show of honour will not represent the true Church of God. Rather, it will retain from the common principles of sincere religion much that is signified by the golden cup. Yet that very cup was full of abominations and the filth of her spiritual fornication: for although she keeps the truth in many respects, by which, as by an enticement, she lies in wait for the credulous and lures them into love of herself, she will nevertheless taint it with the pestilent poison of her heresies and traditions and with the impurity of her spiritual adultery, as was said before. 5. And on her forehead a mystery was written: Babylon the Great, namely that spiritual Babylon (as above), mother of fornications and abominations of the earth. For the heresies and corruptions which are the greatest of all, and which alone are almost worthy to be called chief, will be born from her, and these, carried under the specious title of Christianity, will defile others beyond the rest, right up to the consummation of the age, those on whose lips this voice floats, Lord, Lord. Babylon will not merely bear these errors as a mother; she will also, as a nurse, cherish, nourish and protect them. This is called a mystery because, although it is set out in public and open to the eyes of all (as the inscription on the forehead indicates), only those will be granted to see this wickedness from whose eyes the cataract has been removed by the help of divine mercy. 6. And I saw that woman drunk with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus the Saviour. For she will thirst without measure, without reason or mercy, and most greedily drink the blood of the saints, as you have often heard before; and when I saw her I greatly marvelled at her, for I could not penetrate with understanding the seven heads and ten horns of the beast on which she sat. 7. So the angel who had shown her to me (as you perceived before), seeing that I was struck with astonishment, said: Do not wonder; I will reveal to you the mystery of the woman and of the beast which carries her, which has seven heads and ten horns. 8. This beast which you saw, or the monarchy signified by it (for the fourth monarchy is meant, that most powerful of all and once most flourishing), was, and is not: so greatly is its former power now diminished that it can in some sense be said not to exist; but it will rise again out of the abyss when the first wound to its head has been healed, and yet it will not escape the impending ruin. The inhabitants of the earth, whose names have not been written in the book of life before the foundation of the world, will be seized with wonder at all these things which you have perceived before: they will marvel, I say, at the beast which was (namely flourishing and powerful), and is not (in some measure, as you have just heard), and yet is (namely still resting on its foundations, though much weaker than before). 9. Prick up your ears at what I am about to tell you, for here the wisdom of men will be tested as on a touchstone, so that by my words they may understand which monarchy, which tyranny, is described here. The seven heads of the beast signify seven mountains on which the august seat of this Empire is founded, and seven kings, or as many kinds of magistracy, which this monarchy has used before and will use hereafter. 10. Five of them have been; one is now, namely the sixth; another will follow, namely the seventh; but it has not yet come, and when it comes it will remain for a very short time. 11. The beast which was (namely so powerful) and is not (as you have just heard, for it is now declining) is that eighth, and yet one of the seven. For this beast, raised from the ruins of the fourth monarchy (as has now been explained), since it is about to usurp a heretical tyranny over men's consciences, is distinguished from the others by this new kind of polity; and for this reason it is called the eighth. Nevertheless, because it obtains the same seat of empire as the others, and will rule the world with equal or greater pride, and finally will use the same form of civil polity as each of those seven, I count this beast too among the seven, on account of this, I say, so manifold resemblance. 12. The ten horns which you saw signify ten kings, namely the numerous magistrates in the individual provinces, subordinate to this fourth monarchy, who have not yet received their kingdom. For under all those kinds of polity by which that Empire will be varied, except this last and heretical one, the lesser and subordinate magistrates will be counted among the subjects; but when the beast receives royal power, namely at the time when that Apollyon is raised from the ashes of the fourth beast, from the ruins, I say, of the fourth monarchy, at once the kings of the earth will submit themselves to him in servitude, as subordinate magistrates. Yet before that time the strength of that monarchy lay only in the subjects of the empire; and so the horns, or powers of that beast, before the wound was received, consisted purely of subjects. But when that wound has been healed, the kings and emperors of this world will become the horns and strength of it. 13. These will be of one mind, and will hand over their power and authority to the beast, of their own accord.

units.la: PARAPHRASIS VATICINII
units.tr: PARAPHRASE OF THE PROPHECY

units.la: Babylonico jugo colla præbebunt, & omnes potentiæ suæ nervos in hujus tyrannidis incolumitatem, & Sanctorum vexationem intendent. 14. Et cum agno manum conserent, dum sic illius membra affligunt. Verùm successu destituentur omnes eorum conatus: nam profligabuntur demùm ab Agno: quia ipse est Rex Regum, & Dominus dominantium: & qui ab illius sunt partibus, ejúsque sequuntur castra, ELECTI nominantur & FIDELES. 15. Dixit prætereà mihi Angelus: aquæ illæ, super quibus meretricem sedentem vidisti, populi sunt, & turbæ, & gentes, & linguæ, quæ se illius imperio permiscerunt. 16. Quod autem illa decem cornua attinet, quæ vidisti, hoc saltem tibi prædictum volo: licet ad tempus, libertatis suæ immemores, servituri sint Reges Babyloni, dextris suis ei commodatis ad perfectionem Sanctorum; dies tamen veniet, etiam ante consummationem Universi, quum meretricem, quæ eorum simplicitate tam diu & tam impotenter abusa est, internecino odio prosequentur; solâmque destituent. Cives enim suos & populos, quibus ejus subnixa erat potentia, ejus subtrahent imperio: tum carnes ejus comedent: & ipsam igne exurent; nempe opibus, & potestate, & magnificentia illam exuent: & demùm penitùs evertent. 17. Sed tu noli illud mirari: nam Deus dedit in corda ipsorum; nempe ad tempus eos <bl>Bestia</bl> permisit abutendos; ut nihil agant nisi ex illius libidine: omnes illius prætextus & versutias approbent: regna denique sua illius impotentiæ tantisper permittant, donec verbum Dei consummetur: nempe, illi sua submittent sceptra, & jus regnandi ab illa mendicabunt, dum veniet tempus hoc vaticinio præfixum: quo tempore à Deo excitabuntur Reges ad exscindendam Babylonem: nec enim minus summorum Regum, quàm imæ plebis corda in manu Domini sunt; ut illius exequantur imperia; & tanquam pilæ, quocúnque tandem voluntatis divinæ tulerit impetus, rotentur. 18. Et hæc MULIER vel MERETRIX, quam vidisti, est magna urbs illa Bestiæ, vel Monarchiæ sedes; quæ Regibus terræ cum imperio præest: ut antè tibi innotuit. Cæterùm, in una hac regni sede plures, imò permulti Reges, continuatâ successione, alii alios sequentur, qui eandem religionis hæresin, eosdem superstitionis ritus, & eandem omnes politiam retinebunt; & id quartæ Monarchiæ, unde originem trahet, ænulatione.
units.tr: They will submit their necks to the Babylonian yoke, and will direct all the strength of their power to securing this tyranny and to harassing the saints. 14. And they will join battle with the Lamb, while they afflict his members in this way. But all their efforts will come to nothing, for in the end they will be overthrown by the Lamb, because he is King of kings and Lord of lords. Those who are on his side and follow his camp are called the CHOSEN and the FAITHFUL. 15. Moreover, the angel said to me: the waters on which you saw the harlot sitting are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues, which have yielded themselves to her rule. 16. As for the ten horns that you saw, I wish this at least to be foretold to you: although for a time the kings of Babylon, forgetful of their freedom, will serve her and will lend their right hands to her for the perfecting of the saints, a day will nevertheless come, even before the consummation of the universe, when they will pursue with deadly hatred the harlot who has so long and so shamelessly abused their simplicity, and they will forsake her alone. For they will withdraw their citizens and peoples, on whose support her power rested, from her rule; then they will eat her flesh and burn her with fire; that is, they will strip her of her wealth, her power and her splendour, and at last utterly overthrow her. 17. But do not marvel at this, for God has put it into their hearts; that is, he has allowed the Beast to abuse them for a time, so that they do nothing except at its pleasure. They will approve all its pretexts and cunning devices; they will, in the end, allow their kingdoms to remain under its power for so long as the word of God is fulfilled. Namely, they will submit their sceptres to it and beg from it the right to reign, until the time fixed by this prophecy comes, at which time God will rouse the kings to destroy Babylon. For the hearts of the highest kings are no less in the hand of the Lord than those of the lowest commoners, so that they may carry out his commands, and be rolled like balls wherever the impulse of the divine will finally carries them. 18. And this WOMAN or HARLOT whom you saw is that great city, the seat of the Beast or monarchy, which presides over the kings of the earth with power, as was made known to you before. Moreover, in this one seat of the kingdom there will be many, indeed very many, kings, in unbroken succession, one following another, who will keep the same heresy in religion, the same rites of superstition, and the same polity; and they will do so out of emulation of the fourth monarchy, from which it will derive its origin.

units.la: CAPUT
units.tr: CHAPTER

units.la: DE BABYLONE MAGNA.
units.tr: DE BABYLONE MAGNA.

units.la: CAPUT XVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII.

units.la: Luctus Orbis in ruina Papatus: quae commoda hominibus hujus mundi ex prosperis Papae rebus redundárint: ingentes illius Ecclesiae divitiae & opulentia: animarum nundinatio per indulgentias: caelites de ejus exitio interea temporis laetantur, dum mundus & mundani homines eapropter incedunt pullati.
units.tr: The grief of the world at the fall of the Papacy: what advantages flowed to the men of this world from the prosperity of the Pope's affairs; the immense riches and opulence of that Church; the sale of souls through indulgences; meanwhile the heavenly beings rejoice at its destruction, while the world and worldly men go about clothed in mourning for this reason.

units.la: 1. Et post haec vidi alium Angelum, descendentem de coelo, habentem authoritatem magnam, ita ut terra illius gloriâ illustraretur: nam ut primum Deus per unum e septem Angelis, qui phialas tenebant, faeminam illam bestiae insidentem mihi, quàm antea, fecisset notiorem; nunc per alium quendam, qui est ipse Christus, meritissimam Babylonis damnationem mihi indicat: immo verò Orbi terrarum promulgat, quod Angeli in terram descensu significatur. 2. Exclamavit autem magna voce, dicens: cecidit, cecidit Babylon; illa magna; & facta est domicilium Daemoniorum, & omnium impurarum, dirarúmque volucrium: nempe magna illa Urbs, augusta sedes imperii, excindetur à fundamentis: & aeternum desolabitur, quemadmodum & Hierosolymis olim praedictum fuit. 3. quia ex vino scortationis ejus, omnes gentes biberunt, & Reges terrae cum ea scortati sunt; & mercatores terrae, opibus luxûs ejus ditati sunt; tantâ humanae gloriae magnificentiâ & pompâ splendebat haec Monarchia. 4. Et audivi aliam vocem de coelo, nempe Sancti Spiritus, dicentem: exite ex ea populè mi: omnes inquam electi: ne participes sitis peccatorum ejus, & plagarum, quae propterea illi incutientur: nam si externa tantum conversatione illi cohaerea-tis, & ad ejus flagitia tantum connivere videamini; profectò omnium ejus peccatorum rei peragemini: nam si vobis in votis est, ut Christus in novissimo die palam, & coram Patre suo & Angelis, vos agnoscat, corporáque & animas aeternae felicitatis praemio mactet; non debet esse vobis pudori, coram hominibus & corpore & anima illi servire: hoc ego vos praemonitos volo, ut qui secus facturi sunt, reddantur inexcusabiles. 5. Nam ad eam altitudinem venerunt ejus peccata, ut coelum contingant, & eorum memor est Deus: itaque non solùm deserenda vobis est ejus consuetudo, ut antè monui (neque enim sufficit abstinere à malo.) 6. Sed etiam de vindicta ab ea poscenda cogitandum est; ut id illi reddatis, quod vobis fecit; & duplum illi suorum operum rependatis; & in poculo, quod aliis propinavit, duplum ei propinetis: omnia nempe experiamini, quae ad ejus molestiam & interitum sa-cere cere videbuntur; quemadmodum illa aliis vexandis subvertendisque semper fuit intenta: denique ejus superbiam,& luxuriam tormentis, mœrore, luctu compen-sate. 7. Dicit enim in corde suo, Sedeo Regina, & jam firmatâ meâ Monarchiâ, secura: neque vidua sum: neque orba unquam ero: neque luctûs videbo incommoda: nec interitûs pericula gustabo. 8. Quandoquidem igitur humanis opibus subnixa ejus felicitas, humanis etiam manibus punietur, morte, luctu, fame, incendio; nempe omnes experta tormentorum gradus, denique funditùs peribit: quia validus est Dominus Deus, qui damnabit eam. 9. Tum Reges terræ, olim cornua illius, quique cum illa fcortati & luxuriati sunt, conspecto incendii fumo, præ miseratione flebunt & lugebunt eam: quanquam enim illi ipsi auctores ruinæ hujus extiterint, ut jam explicatum est; tanta tamen ea futura est, ut quum fumantes aspexerunt cineres, animi eorum in miserationem conversi, non possint non deplorare, quod manus peregerint. 10. Stabunt autem procul à tormentis ejus: refricabitur enim tormentis hisce peccatorum suorum memoria, quæ illis ingentem incutient pavorem: & admiratione perculsi dicent: vah, vah! magna illa Urbs BABYLON, Urbs illa valida, cujus judicium & interitus unâ & eádem horâ, & simul venere. 11. Et mercatores flebunt & lugebunt illam; quia merces eorum non ementur amplius. : ejus enim pompa vendibiles faciebat pretiosas merces, unde mercatores ditescebant. 12. quales sunt aurum, argentum, gemmæ, margaritæ, byssus, purpura, sericum, coccus; & omnia vasorum genera idololatriæ inservientia, ex ebore, ligno pretioso, ære, ferro, marmore. 13. Cinnamomum & suffitus omnijuges, ad superstitiosos ritus; cum unguentis & thure, ad eandem rem, & similia; & omne genus frumenti, jumentisque; & oves ad conviviorum apparatus; & equi, & currus, & mancipia; & triumphorum & processionum solennitates, & hominum animas: nam multos conducet institores animarum, qui indulgentias; queis animæ sospitari, redimi, & liberari creduntur; pretio distrahant. Sed brevi de his posteà. 14. Et fructus desiderio-rum animæ tuæ, ô Babylon, abibunt à te: vertent nimirum in mœrorem lubentiæ tuæ: & oblectamenta, & omnia pinguia, & præclara abierunt à te: omnia nempe tua emolumenta & voluptates te destituent: nec amplius illa invenies: tuum enim nomen in æternum delebitur. 15. Et mercatores, qui harum mercium emtione venditionéque ditabuntur, procul stabunt à tormentis ejus, flentes & lugentes. 16. Vah, vah, dicent: magna illa Urbs olim amiciebatur bysso, purpurâ, &, cocco, auróque deaurata, & gemmis, & margaritis ornata, intuentium oculos præstinguebat: ecce, unâ horâ vastatæ sunt ejus divitiæ: omnisque ejus pompa disparuit. 17. Et omnes gubernatores, & navarchi, omnisque in navibus versantium turba; & omnes nautæ, & quotquot ex mari quæstum faciunt, procul stabunt, præ timore: 18. & clamabunt videntes fumum incendii ejus; dicentes cum magna admiratione; qua urbs magnificentia aut gloria splendore hanc æquabat ? 19. Et miseratione ruinæ ejus, & mœrore amissi proprii quæstûs, quem, mercibus undiquáque in eam Urbem advehendis, facere solebant, capitibus suis pulverem injicient, & cineres: Vah, vah, ajentes, quòd magna illa Urbs; in qua omnes, qui habebant naves in mari, mercium pretiï & negotiandi privilegio locupletati sunt; unâ horâ desolata est. 20. At quanquam in ejus funere mœsti futuri sint terreni homines, propter terrenarum voluptatum & quæstuum jacturam, quibus illi Babylonis ope ante fruebantur; cujus religio omnis terrena erat, nempe humanis inventis & traditionibus nixa, terrenâque pompâ & potentiâ sustentata: exultate tamen cæli in ejus interitu: Væsque, Sancti Apostoli & Prophetæ, lætamini: nam in ejus supplicio vestram Deus vindicavit injuriam. 21. Tùm verò ad firmandum Babylonicæ ruinæ vaticinium, vidi Angelum validum tollere vastum lapidem, instar molaris, eúmque projicere in mare, dicentem: Tanto certè cum impetu dejicietur Babylon, illa magna Urbs: neque amplius locus ejus invenietur: quemadmodum de altera illa & corporea Babylone vaticinatus est Jeremias: 22. & vox citharædorum, & Musicorum, & tibiá & tubá canentium non amplius audietur in te: omnis enim lætitia & hilaritas ex hac Monarchia, ejúsque sede exulabit: nec ullus artifex, cujuscúnque artis, amplius invenietur in te: nec sonitus mola amplius audietur in te: nam incolarum honore hæc Urbs inposterum destituetur. 23. Nec lucernæ lux amplius invenietur in te: neque mariti & uxoris vox amplius audietur in te: nam ut impiis nullus ibi inposterum futurus est locus; sic nulla erunt piorum domicilia: adeò omnibus devovebitur diris, ut nec virginum lampades ibi arsuræ sint; nec Christus cum Sponsa Ecclesia, unquam apparituras; quanquam in media tyrannide etiam intra illius Urbis pòmœria electorum nonnulli semper latuerint, & semper quóque futuri sint, cujus Urbis mercatores crant optimates terræ, cujúsque præstigiis omnes gentes à vero seducti sunt. 24. Et sanguis Prophetarum & Sanctorum in ea inventus est, & omnium qui mactati sunt in terra. Jure igitur hac clade delebitur Babylon; tum quia nuncios suos & legatos magna instructos potestate insitores indulgentiarum suarum esse voluit; precúmque, & Sacramentorum, & meritorum, & peccatorum, & ipsarum quóque animarum, ut antè audivistis: atque ita multis gentibus hoc tanquam carmine fucum fecit: tum quia barbarè Sanctos afflixit, & interemit; adeò ut omnium, ab Abele, Sanctorum sanguinem, qui vitam suam pro divinæ veritatis amore, & testimonio Filii, tánquam victimam obtulerunt, ab illa sit exacturus Deus, & in illam vindicaturus: ut quæ priorum tyrannorum furorem in persequendis & opprimendis Sanctis exceperit, æquârit, excesserit.
units.tr: 1. And after these things I saw another Angel coming down from heaven, having great authority, so that the earth was lit up with his glory. For when God, through one of the seven Angels who held the vials, had earlier made that woman who sits upon the beast better known to me, now, through another, who is Christ himself, he shows me the most deserved condemnation of Babylon; or rather, he proclaims it to the whole world, which is signified by the Angel's descent to the earth. 2. And he cried out with a loud voice, saying: Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, and she has become a habitation of demons, and a hold of every unclean and hateful bird: namely, that great city, the august seat of empire, will be torn up from its foundations and will be laid waste forever, just as was foretold long ago of Jerusalem. 3. For all nations have drunk of the wine of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth have grown rich from the riches of her luxury; so splendidly did this monarchy shine with the magnificence and pomp of human glory. 4. And I heard another voice from heaven, namely that of the Holy Spirit, saying: Come out of her, my people: all of you, I say, the elect, so that you may not share in her sins and in the plagues that will therefore be inflicted on her. For if you merely cling to her in outward conduct and seem to connive only at her wickedness, you will certainly be made guilty of all her sins. For if it is your desire that Christ, on the last day, openly and before his Father and the Angels, acknowledge you and reward your bodies and souls with the prize of eternal happiness, you ought not to be ashamed to serve him, in body and in soul, before men. I want you to be warned of this beforehand, so that those who would act otherwise may be made inexcusable. 5. For her sins have reached such a height that they touch heaven, and God remembers them. Therefore you must not only abandon her customs, as I warned before (for it is not enough to abstain from evil). 6. But you must also think about exacting vengeance from her, so that you may pay her back what she has done to you, and repay her double for her works, and pour out for her double in the cup which she has poured out for others. Indeed, try everything that seems suited to her harassment and destruction, just as she was always intent on harassing and overthrowing others; in short, repay her pride and her luxury with torments, mourning, and grief. 7. For she says in her heart, I sit as queen, and, my monarchy now secure, I am not a widow, nor shall I ever be bereaved, nor shall I see the troubles of mourning: nor shall I taste the dangers of destruction. 8. Since, therefore, her happiness, which rests on human resources, will also be punished by human hands, with death, mourning, famine, and fire; having experienced every degree of torment, she will at last perish utterly, because the Lord God who will condemn her is mighty. 9. Then the kings of the earth, who once were her horns, and who committed fornication and luxury with her, when they see the smoke of the burning, will weep and mourn for her out of pity. For although they themselves were the authors of this ruin, as has now been explained, nevertheless it will be so great that when they behold the smoking ashes, their minds, turned to pity, cannot help but lament that they carried out the deed. 10. They will stand, however, far from her torments, for the memory of their sins will be reopened by these torments, and this will strike them with immense terror; and struck with amazement they will say: Alas, alas! That great city Babylon, that mighty city, whose judgment and destruction came together, in one and the same hour. 11. And the merchants will weep and mourn over her, because their wares will no longer be bought. For her pomp made precious wares saleable, by which the merchants grew rich. 12. Such wares are gold, silver, gems, pearls, fine linen, purple, silk, scarlet; and all kinds of vessels used in idolatry, of ivory, precious wood, bronze, iron, marble. 13. Cinnamon and incense of every kind for superstitious rites; with ointments and frankincense for the same purpose, and the like; and every kind of grain and beasts of burden; and sheep for the preparation of banquets; and horses, and chariots, and slaves; and the solemnities of triumphs and processions, and the souls of men: for she will hire many dealers in souls, who will sell at a price indulgences, by which souls are believed to be saved, redeemed, and freed. But more of this shortly. 14. And the fruits your soul desired, O Babylon, will depart from you; they will indeed turn into grief for your delight; and your delights and all your rich and splendid things have departed from you; all your gains and pleasures will desert you, and you will never find them again, for your name will be blotted out forever. 15. And the merchants who grew rich from buying and selling these wares will stand far from her torments, weeping and mourning. 16. Alas, alas, they will say: that great city, once clothed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet, gilded with gold, and adorned with gems and pearls, dazzled the eyes of onlookers: behold, in one hour her riches have been laid waste, and all her pomp has vanished. 17. And all the pilots and shipmasters, and the whole crowd of those who sail in ships, and all the sailors, and as many as make their living from the sea, will stand far off, for fear. 18. And they will cry out, seeing the smoke of her burning, saying with great astonishment: what city was ever equal to this in magnificence or splendor of glory? 19. And in pity for her ruin, and in grief at the loss of their own gain, which they used to make from the wares brought from every side to that city, they will throw dust and ashes on their heads, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, in which all who had ships on the sea were enriched by the price of goods and the privilege of trade, has been laid desolate in one hour. 20. But although earthly men will be sorrowful at her funeral, because of the loss of the earthly pleasures and gains which they used to enjoy through Babylon's help, whose whole religion was earthly, resting on human inventions and traditions and sustained by earthly pomp and power, nevertheless rejoice, O heavens, at her destruction. Rejoice, holy apostles and prophets, for in her punishment God has avenged your injury. 21. Then indeed, to confirm the prophecy of Babylon's ruin, I saw a mighty Angel take up a huge stone, like a millstone, and throw it into the sea, saying: With such violence will Babylon, that great city, be cast down, and no place for her will be found again; just as Jeremiah prophesied of that other, bodily Babylon. 22. and the voice of harpers, and of musicians, and of those who play the pipe and the trumpet, will be heard no more in you: for all joy and merriment will depart from this monarchy and from its seat; and no craftsman of any craft will be found in you any more; nor will the sound of the millstone be heard in you any more; for this city will be deprived of the honor of its inhabitants from now on. 23. Nor will the light of a lamp be found in you any more; nor will the voice of bridegroom and bride be heard in you any more; for just as there will be no place for the wicked there in future, so there will be no dwelling for the righteous; so completely will she be devoted to every curse, that the lamps of the virgins will not burn there, nor will Christ ever appear there with his bride, the Church; although in the midst of tyranny, even within the walls of that city, some of the elect have always lain hidden and always will, that city whose merchants were the nobles of the earth, and by whose enchantments all nations have been led astray from the truth. 24. And the blood of the prophets and saints was found in her, and of all who have been slain on the earth. Therefore Babylon will rightly be destroyed by this calamity; both because she wished her messengers and legates, armed with great power, to be the sellers of her indulgences, and of prayers, and of sacraments, and of merits, and of sins, and even of souls themselves, as you heard before; and thus with this song, as it were, she has deceived many nations; and because she has cruelly afflicted and slain the saints, so that God will exact from her, and avenge upon her, the blood of all the saints from Abel onward, who offered their lives as a sacrifice for love of divine truth and for the testimony of the Son. She has matched, equaled, and surpassed the fury of the earlier tyrants in persecuting and oppressing the saints.

units.la: CAPUT XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: Sancti Deum laudant ob Papæ exitium: Gloria secundi adventûs Christi fusè explicata. Papæ ejúsque Ecclesiæ æterna damnatio.
units.tr: The saints praise God for the destruction of the Pope. The glory of Christ's second coming is set out at length. The eternal damnation of the Pope and his Church.

units.la: 1. Igitur juxta illa monita, quibus cœli & cælites, Prophetæ nempe & Apostoli, tam jubebantur lætari de interitu Babylonis, quàm reprobi mœrebant, ut suprà audivistis: juxta illa inquam monita, magnæ concionis vocem in cœlo audivi, dicentem: HALLELUJAH, quod si interpreteris sonat; Laudate Dominum, alta voce: salus, honor, gloria & virtus omnis cum Deo nostro. 2. Nam vera & justa sunt ejus judicia: ille MERETRICEM illam magnam, quæ scortatione terram polluerat, damnavit; & suâ dextrâ sanguinem servorum suorum in illam vindicavit. 3. Deinde secundò dixerunt: HALLELUJAH: nam fumus ruinæ illius ascendit in omnia secula: neque enim unquam resurget: sed vigili igne semper ardebit. 4. Itidem viginti quatuor Seniores, ut Deo gratias agerent, prociderunt in facies suas: & cum illis quatuor Bestiæ adorârunt Deum insidentem throno, uno ore dicentes omnes: amen, hallelujah. 5. Vocem quoque à throno prodeuntem audivi; nimirum unius è bestiis, ei succollantibus dicentem: Laudate Deum nostrum omnes servi ejus, & qui timetis cum parvi & magni. 6. Et flatim juxta hoc mandatum appulit ad aures meas vox, quasi condensæ concionis, similis multarum aquarum, aut tonitrui fragoribus, dicens: HALLELUJAH: quoniam Dominus Deus noster, dirata Babylone, ejúsque civibus oppressis, suum adiit regnum. 7. Gaudeamus igitur, & exultemus: illique omnem demus gloriam; quia venerunt NUPTIÆ AGNI, nempe dies novissimus prope est: & EJUS UXOR paravit se illi: scilicet ejus Ecclesia ab improborum contagione liberata est. 8. Et datum est ei, ut amictetur bysso munda, & splendida, quæ est justificatio sanctorum: nam ut puritas, splendor, candor. & pretium commendant byssum; sic intaminatus ille est, & carus, & gloriosus justitiæ per imputationem amictus, quo vestiuntur Sancti: nam ex sola Christi justitia texitur ille nostræ justificationis amictus, die novissimo induendus; quem quóque ab ipso porrigi necesse est, ut modò audivistis: nam quemadmodum ne bona quidem cogitatio in nostra est potestate; ita penes nos non est nisi æternam mortem merèri: & cùm omnibus bonis operibus, quæ possumus, defuncti sumus, id nobis exstimandum relinquitur, nos inutiles esse servos, ut Christus ipse dixit. 9. Tunc eadem vox, nempe Angeli, qui hæc exposuit, dixit mihi: Scribe & prode posterorum memoriæ: beati qui ad cœnam nuptiarum AGNI vocati sunt: quarum ex ipsius ore parabolam audivistis: nam quotquot efficaciter vocati sunt, nunquam rejicientur, sed in æternum electi sunt: & dixit mihi, vera sunt hæc verba Dei, quæ te jussi posterorum memoriæ scripta relinquere: nempe ab ipso Deo profectum est hujus promissionis solatium, quam ita distinctim voluti fratribus tuis tuâ operâ testatam: nam in novissimis diebus hæc ipsa meretricia & hæretica Babylon hujus promissionis fidem apud suos elevabit, & homines electionis suæ incertitudine ambiguos suspendet. 10. Et procidi ante pedes Angeli, adoraturus illum (nam omnes mortales naturæ vitio in rerum visibilium cultum, id est, idololatriam propensi sunt: ea est nostræ carnis infirmitas, nisi cœlitùs divinæ gratiæ fultentetur fulcro) verùm ille ægrè ferens, vide, inquit, ne feceris: nam quanquam Creatoris beneficio, Angelicæ naturæ excellentia vincat humanam, conservus tuus nihilominus sum, atque adeò unus è fratribus tuis, creatura, & minister Christi, ejus testimonio defungens in cœlis; quemadmodum tu in terris. Unum igitur Deum adora: siquidem nullam creaturam cultu aut prece nostra fas est dignari; neque verò ulla est, nisi per Christum, intercessio: nec est, quod mihi hujus Prophetiæ gratiâ divinum exhibeas honorem: testimonium enim Jesu est Spiritus Prophetiæ, quod donum mihi cum multis commune est: imò verò non est alius, quàm Prophetiæ Spiritus, qui gratiâ instruit omnes electos, ut verè & constanter de Christo testificentur; licet hoc non sit illius Spiritûs donum, quo prædicuntur futura.
units.tr: 1. Therefore, in accordance with those admonitions by which the heavens and the heavenly ones, that is the prophets and apostles, were bidden to rejoice at the destruction of Babylon, just as the reprobate mourned, as you heard above, I heard in heaven the voice of a great multitude saying: HALLELUJAH, which, if you interpret it, means: Praise the Lord with a loud voice: salvation, honour, glory and all power belong to our God. 2. For his judgments are true and just: he has condemned that great HARLOT, who polluted the earth with her fornication, and with his right hand he has avenged the blood of his servants upon her. 3. Then a second time they said: HALLELUJAH: for the smoke of her ruin rises for ever and ever; she will never rise again, but will always burn with an unquenchable fire. 4. Likewise the twenty-four Elders fell on their faces to give thanks to God, and with them the four Beasts worshipped God sitting on the throne, all saying with one voice: amen, hallelujah. 5. I also heard a voice coming forth from the throne, namely of one of the beasts, speaking to those who supported it: Praise our God, all you his servants, and you who fear him, both small and great. 6. And at once, in accordance with this command, there came to my ears a voice like that of a gathered multitude, like the sound of many waters or the crashing of thunder, saying: HALLELUJAH: for the Lord our God, having condemned Babylon and oppressed her citizens, has entered upon his kingdom. 7. Let us therefore rejoice and exult, and give him all glory, for the MARRIAGE OF THE LAMB has come; that is, the last day is near, and HIS WIFE has made herself ready for him: that is, his Church has been freed from the contagion of the wicked. 8. And it was given to her to be clothed in fine linen, clean and bright, which is the justification of the saints. For as purity, brightness and whiteness commend linen and give it its worth, so that garment of righteousness which is imputed, and in which the saints are clothed, is undefiled, precious and glorious. For that garment of our justification, to be put on on the last day, is woven from the righteousness of Christ alone, and it is necessary that it too be supplied by him, as you have just heard. For just as not even a good thought is in our power, so it is not in us to deserve anything but eternal death; and since we have come to the end of all the good works we are able to do, what remains for us is to acknowledge that we are unprofitable servants, as Christ himself said. 9. Then the same voice, namely that of the Angel who set out these things, said to me: Write and hand down to the memory of posterity: blessed are those who are called to the supper of the marriage of the LAMB; you heard the parable of this from his own mouth. For all who are effectually called will never be rejected, but are chosen for eternity. And he said to me: these are the true words of God, which I have been bidden to leave written for the memory of posterity. The comfort of this promise has come from God himself, and you have set it out so distinctly and attested it for your brothers by your labour. For in the last days this very harlot and heretical Babylon will weaken faith in this promise among her own, and will keep men wavering, uncertain of their election. 10. And I fell down at the feet of the Angel, intending to worship him. (For all mortals, by the vice of nature, are inclined to the worship of visible things, that is, to idolatry; such is the weakness of our flesh, unless it is propped up by the prop of divine grace from heaven.) But he, taking it ill, said: see, do not do it: for although by the Creator's kindness the excellence of the angelic nature surpasses the human, nevertheless I am your fellow servant, and so one of your brothers, a creature and minister of Christ, discharging his testimony in heaven just as you do on earth. Therefore worship the one God: for it is not right that any creature be honoured with our worship or prayer, nor is there any intercession except through Christ. Nor is there any reason why you should render me divine honour on account of this prophecy: for the testimony of Jesus is the Spirit of prophecy, a gift that I share with many. Indeed it is none other than the Spirit of prophecy, who by grace instructs all the elect so that they bear true and steadfast witness concerning Christ, although this is not that gift of the Spirit by which future things are foretold.

units.la: I. Enter Proverbia Salomonis à viris Regis Ezechiæ collecta, & ordine primum, & sensus præstantia minimè postremum est, quod Proverb. xxv. 2. extat, his verbis: כבוד אלהים הסתר דבר וכבוד מלכים חקר דבר. Gloria Dei est occultare verbum, & gloria Regum scrutari verbum. Conferuntur invicem Rex in Cœlis supremus, & Reges summates in terris. Illi gloriosum, amplumque statuitur, occultare sermonem, non quòd ad gloriam ejus pertineat, ita occultare verbum, quo salutis negotium nobis revelatur, ut à quovis fideli, Spiritu Dei prædito sine humana ope, ex ipso Dei verbo intelligi nequeat; sed quòd magnificum Deo sit ita proponere verbum suum, ut sine attentione, discretione spirituali, & scrutatione, intelligi ad salutem nequeat. Unde Deus Israël salvator vocatur אל מסתתר Deus occultans se Esai. xlv. 15. His verò, Regibus terrenis gloriosum statuitur, scrutari sermonem, puta eundem à Deo occultatum, nec non alia ad regium munus pertinentia, ita videlicet, ut reverenter, devotè & sagaciter illa legant, scrutentur, & in adyta sensuum divinorum revelati verbi penetrare unicè contendant.
units.tr: I. Among the Proverbs of Solomon, collected by the men of King Hezekiah, the first place belongs to this one, and it is by no means the least in the excellence of its sense, which stands in Proverbs 25:2 in these words: כבוד אלהים הסתר דבר וכבוד מלכים חקר דבר. It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, and the glory of kings to search out a matter. The supreme King in heaven and the great kings on earth are compared with one another. For God, it is glorious and grand to conceal the word, not in the sense that it belongs to his glory to hide the word by which the business of salvation is revealed to us, so that it cannot be understood from the word of God itself by any faithful person endowed with the Spirit of God without human help; but it is magnificent for God so to set forth his word that it cannot be understood unto salvation without attention, spiritual discernment and searching. Hence God is called the saviour of Israel, אל מסתתר, a God who hides himself, Isaiah 45:15. But for earthly kings it is glorious to search out the word, namely the same word concealed by God, and other matters pertaining to the royal office; that is, to read and search these reverently, devoutly and shrewdly, and to strive only to penetrate into the inner sanctuaries of the divine senses of the revealed word.

units.la: II. Solus nempe Deus, coram cujus oculis omnia præterita, præsentia & futura sunt γυμνὰ καὶ τετραχηλισμένα nuda & resupinata Hebr. iv. 13. expeditè, promptè & infallibiliter uno intuitu, adeóque sine חקר pervestigatione, scrutatione propriè dicta ita cognoscit, ut tanquam in speculo lucidissimo ipsi splendescant omnia. Unde David ψ. cxxxix. 6. פלאיה רעת ממני נשגבה לא אוכל לה. Mirabilis est scientia (tua) præ me sublimis est, non possum eam attingere. Homines vero omnes, adeoque Reges etiam animales quidem, plane ea quae Spiritus sunt, non capiunt 1 Cor. II. 14. Spirituales vero etiam spiritualia sine labore, industria, sagacitate & scrutatione verbi revelati, ita ut ad salutem intelligentia proficiat, non penetrant.
units.tr: II. Certainly only God, before whose eyes all things past, present and future are γυμνὰ καὶ τετραχηλισμένα, [naked and laid open], Hebrews 4:13, knows them readily, promptly and infallibly in a single glance, and so without any חקר, that is, without investigation properly so called, such that all things shine in him as in the clearest mirror. Hence David, Psalm 139:6: פלאיה רעת ממני נשגבה לא אוכל לה. Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain to it. But all men, and therefore kings too, natural men indeed, do not receive the things of the Spirit of God, 1 Cor. 2:14. And spiritual men do not penetrate spiritual things without labour, diligence, shrewdness and the searching of the revealed word, so that understanding may advance to salvation.

units.la: III. Id vero cum in omni revelatione Divina, tum in ea maxime, qua futura Ecclesiae fata consignantur, usu venit. Ita enim Deus futura ab antiquo (Esai. XLV. 21.) revelat, ut tamen occultet, hactenus videlicet, ut praedictorum sensus ex verbo praedicente & eventu rei, omni opera industriaque investigari debeat.
units.tr: III. This happens not only in every divine revelation but especially in that by which the future fates of the Church are recorded. For thus God reveals the future from of old (Isaiah 45:21), yet conceals it, to this extent, namely, that the sense of what has been foretold must be sought out with all effort and diligence, from the foretelling word and from the outcome of the event.

units.la: IV. Ejusmodi Occultata Divinitus, seu μυστήρια cum plurima divina Apocalypsis Johannis complectatur, inter ea haud postremum certe locum obtinet μυστήριον, Babylon magna, mater fornicationum & abominationum terrae. Apoc. XVII. 5. Quod si igitur ad gloriam Regum pertinet, etiam illud verbum scrutari, inprimis cum praedictum sit, Reges quosdam cum Babylone scortaturos, adeoque piorum Regum omnium interfuit plurimum, matrem illam fornicationum cognoscere, & ab ejus consuetudine & fascinis abhorrere, non minus ad officium fidelium omnium attinere putemus, ut mysterium isthoc magni, si quod aliud, momenti, compertum maxime habeant. Sic enim brevi compendio rerum maximarum cognitione defungi, & disputationes operosissimas, in quibus sophismatum & aequivocationum fucus regnare potest, redimere dabitur. Incisa radice una cum arbore, surculi omnes prostrati corruunt. Simile pretium hujus etiam operae sperare licet.
units.tr: IV. Since such hidden things, that is, mysteries divinely concealed, make up most of the divine Apocalypse of John, among them certainly not the least place is held by the mystery, Great Babylon, the mother of harlots and of the abominations of the earth (Rev. 17:5). If therefore it belongs to the glory of kings to search out even this word, especially since it has been foretold that certain kings will fornicate with Babylon, then it is of the greatest concern to all pious kings to know that mother of fornications and to shrink from her company and her charms. Nor, we think, is it less the duty of all the faithful that they should have this mystery, if any other, of great moment, thoroughly understood. For in this way they will be able to dispatch the knowledge of the greatest matters in a brief summary, and to be spared those very laborious disputations in which the cloak of sophisms and equivocations can hold sway. Once the root is cut away with the tree, all the shoots fall prostrate. A similar reward may be hoped for from this labour.

units.la: V. Vocatur Babylon & μεγάλη, magna. Apoc. XVI. 19. XVII. 5. XVIII. 2. & πόλις μεγάλη, civitas magna. cap. XIV. 8. XVIII. 16. 18. 21. μεγάλη, ἰσχυρά, magna, robusta. cap. xviii. 10. Ejus verò tum nomen proprium, tum peccatum enorme, tum locus seu sedes, tum judicium gravissimum indigitatur. Nomen proprium in facie ejus scriptum ejusmodi est: μυστήριον. Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν καὶ τῶν βδελυγμάτων τῆς γῆς. Mysterium. Babylon magna, mater fornicationum & abominationum terræ. Apoc. xvii. 5.
units.tr: V. Babylon is called great [μεγάλη], great. Apoc. XVI. 19. XVII. 5. XVIII. 2. and "the great city" [πόλις μεγάλη] cap. XIV. 8. XVIII. 16. 18. 21. Great, mighty, robust [μεγάλη, ἰσχυρά], great, robust. cap. xviii. 10. Her proper name, her enormous sin, her place or seat, and her most grievous judgment are all indicated. Her proper name, written on her forehead, is as follows: "Mystery. Babylon the great, the mother of harlots and of the abominations of the earth" [μυστήριον. Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν καὶ τῶν βδελυγμάτων τῆς γῆς]. Apoc. xvii. 5.

units.la: VI. Peccatum quidem ejus enorme in universum definitur ἁμαρτία ἀγρὶ ἢ ἀδικία peccatum in cœlum, ἀδικήματα injustitiæ. cap. xviii. 5. & βδελύγματα abominationes. cap. xvii. 5. Species verò peccati ejus præcipuæ sunt, scortatio, tyrannis seu crudelitas, blasphemiæ, superbia, veneficia & nundinatio.
units.tr: VI. Her enormous sin is in general defined as sin reaching to heaven [ἁμαρτία ἄχρι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ] or injustice [ἀδικία], injustices [ἀδικήματα]. cap. xviii. 5. and abominations [βδελύγματα] abominationes. cap. xvii. 5. Her principal kinds of sin are fornication, tyranny or cruelty, blasphemies, pride, sorcery and trafficking.

units.la: VII. Quoad scortationem, vocatur μήτηρ μεγάλη meretrix magna cap. xvii. 1. xix. 2. μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν mater fornicationum & abominationum terræ cap. xvii. 2. 5. ἀκαθαρσίας πορνείας immunditia scortationis. cap. xvii. 4. & δυναμις & πλούτος potentia luxuriæ cap. xviii. 3. qua scilicet ispnian luxuriavit. ib. v. 7. Neque scortatio duntaxat & lascivia, sed seductio etiam ad eandem, propinato incolis terræ fornicationum & abominationum philtro, Babyloni tribuitur. Nam ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πεπώκασιν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ex vino excandescentiæ scortationis suæ potavit omnes gentes cap. xiv. 8. Et in manu sua habet aureum poculum γέμον βδελυγμάτων καὶ ἀκαθαρσίας πορνείας αὐτῆς, plenum abominationibus & immunditia scortationis suæ cap. xvii. 4. Adeò quidem, ut Reges ipsi terræ non incolæ tantùm alii philtro isthoc & cramate inebriati cum ea scortati dicantur cap. xvii. 2. xviii. 3. 9.
units.tr: VII. As to fornication, she is called "great harlot" [μήτηρ μεγάλη] meretrix magna cap. xvii. 1. xix. 2., and "mother of fornications and abominations of the earth" mater fornicationum & abominationum terræ cap. xvii. 2. 5., and "the filthiness of fornication" [ἀκαθαρσίας πορνείας] immunditia scortationis cap. xvii. 4., and "the power and wealth" [δυναμις & πλούτος] potentia luxuriæ cap. xviii. 3., by which, of course, she luxuriated [ispnian] luxuriavit ib. v. 7. Babylon is credited not only with fornication and wantonness but also with seducing others to the same, by pouring out for the inhabitants of the earth a philtre of fornications and abominations. For "all the nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath [ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς θυμοῦ] of her fornication" ex vino excandescentiæ scortationis suæ potavit omnes gentes cap. xiv. 8. And she has in her hand a golden cup "full of abominations and the filthiness of her fornication" [γέμον βδελυγμάτων καὶ ἀκαθαρσίας πορνείας αὐτῆς] plenum abominationibus & immunditia scortationis suæ cap. xvii. 4. So much so that even the kings of the earth, not only its inhabitants, are said to have been made drunk with this philtre and this potion, and to have fornicated with her. cap. xvii. 2. xviii. 3. 9.

units.la: VIII. Tyrannis seu Crudelitas Babylonis magnæ inde elucescit, quòd ceu mulier inducitur καθημένη ἐπὶ θηρίον sedens super bestia coccinea cap. xvii. 3. & quidem μεθύουσα ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ ἐκ τὸ αἷμα τῶν μαρτύρων
units.tr: VIII. The tyranny or cruelty of great Babylon is evident from this, that she is introduced as a woman "sitting upon a scarlet beast" [καθημένη ἐπὶ θηρίον κοκκινον] cap. xvii. 3., and indeed "drunk [μεθύουσα] with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs [ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων]."

units.la: Peccata enormia.
units.tr: Enormous sins.

units.la: Scortatio, & adulterium seu seductio. Regum & incolarum terræ.
units.tr: Fornication, and adultery or seduction, of kings and of the inhabitants of the earth.

units.la: Tyrannica crudelitas adversus sanctos. μαρτύρων τ᾽ηες ebria sanguine sanctorum, & sanguine testium Jesu. ib. v. 6. Cujus proin vinum, quo Reges gentium inebriavit, vocatur οἶνος τῆς θυμοῦ vinum excandescentiae. cap. xiv. 8. xviii. 3. Et in quo αἷμα τῶν ἁγίων, τῶν ἁγίων, sanguis Prophetarum & Sanctorum, omniumque in terra maclatorum repertus dicitur. cap. xviii. 24.
units.tr: Tyrannical cruelty against the saints: drunk with the blood of the saints, and the blood of the witnesses of Jesus [μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ]. ib. v. 6. Accordingly her wine, with which she made the kings of the nations drunk, is called wine of wrath [οἶνος τῆς θυμοῦ] cap. xiv. 8. xviii. 3. And in her is found, as it is said, the blood [αἷμα τῶν ἁγίων] of the saints, of the saints [τῶν ἁγίων], the blood of the prophets and saints, and of all who have been slain on the earth cap. xviii. 24.

units.la: IX. Jam & blasphemandi horribile cacoëthes eidem tribuitur, utpote sedenti super bestia plena nominum blasphemiae, cap. xvii. 3. Superbia vero intolerabilis ejus notatur passim. Etenim dicitur περιβεβλημένη πορφύρα καὶ κοκκίνῳ induta purpura & cocco, & inaurata auro, & lapidibus pretiosis & margaritis, habens poculum aureum in manu sua cap. xvii. 3. & xviii. 10. Et inducitur in sinu ac corde suo gaudens, & δοξάζων glorificans se ipsam his verbis: κάθημαι βασίλισσα, καὶ χήρα οὐκ εἰμί, καὶ πένθος οὐ μὴ ἴδω. Sedeo Regina, & vidua non ero, & luctum non videbo. cap. xviii. 7.
units.tr: IX. Moreover, a horrible itch for blasphemy is also ascribed to her, since she sits upon a beast full of names of blasphemy cap. xvii. 3. Her pride, however, is noted everywhere as intolerable. For she is said to be clothed [περιβεβλημένη] in purple and scarlet, gilded with gold, precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand cap. xvii. 3. and xviii. 10. And she is introduced rejoicing in her heart and bosom and glorifying herself [δοξάζων], in these words: "I sit a queen [κάθημαι βασίλισσα], and I am no widow, and I shall not see mourning." cap. xviii. 7.

units.la: X. Sed & Veneficium eidem diserte imputatur, ne mulierem veneficam quandam Circen esse ignoraremus. Nam ἐν τῇ φαρμακίᾳ, veneficio suo omnes gentes seduxisse dicitur cap. xviii. 23. Denique ἐμπορία, nundinatio quaedam eidem clare tribuitur. Quippe mercatores terrae ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως τῆς τρυφῆς ex potentia luxuriae ejus divites facti dicuntur, cap. xviii. 3. Et eversa ac combusta Babylone mercatores terrae ploraturi & planctuři inducuntur, quia merces eorum nemo emit amplius. cap. xviii. 11. Quae merces Babylonicae in sequentibus fuse enumerantur.
units.tr: X. Sorcery too is expressly imputed to her, lest we fail to recognise that she is some sorceress, a Circe. For she is said to have seduced all the nations by her sorcery [ἐν τῇ φαρμακίᾳ], by her witchcraft cap. xviii. 23. Finally, a certain trafficking [ἐμπορία], trade, is clearly attributed to her. Indeed the merchants of the earth are said to have become rich from the power of her luxury, cap. xviii. 3. And when Babylon is overthrown and burned, the merchants of the earth are introduced as weeping and lamenting because no one buys their wares any more. cap. xviii. 11. These Babylonian wares are listed at length in what follows.

units.la: XI. Sedes Babylonis hujus, seu loci qualitas non semel etiam exprimitur. Dicitur enim καθημένη ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων τῶν πολλῶν sedens super aquis multis. cap. xvii. 1. nec non ἐπὶ θηρίον super bestia coccinea. v. 3. quod illam gestans habere dicitur septem capita, & decem cornua. v. 7. septem vero illa capita. v. 9. definiuntur ἑπτὰ ὄρη ἐπ᾽ ἃ ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται. ἐπ᾽ ἀραὐτῶν, septem montes, quibus mulier insidet. Et v. 18. clarius id ita explicatur: Et mulier, quam vidisti, est ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ ἔχουσα βασιλείαν ἐπὶ τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς, Civitas illa magna, quæ obtinet regnum super Regna terræ.
units.tr: XI. The seat of this Babylon, or the quality of her place, is expressed more than once. For she is said to be sitting [καθημένη] upon many waters [ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων τῶν πολλῶν], cap. xvii. 1., and also upon the beast, the scarlet one, v. 3., which she is said to carry, having seven heads and ten horns, v. 7. The seven heads, v. 9., are defined as seven mountains [ἑπτὰ ὄρη], on which the woman sits [ἐπ᾽ ἃ ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται], seven mountains on which the woman sits. And at v. 18. this is explained more clearly: "And the woman whom you saw is the great city [ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη], which has a kingdom over the kings of the earth," that great city which holds dominion over the kingdoms of the earth.

units.la: XII. Iudicium denique Babylonis magnæ per gradus procedit. Decem nempe cornua Bestiæ cui insidet mulier, hoc est, decem Reges meretricem primò odio habituri & derelicturi, ut sit nuda; secundò carnes ejus devoraturi; tertiò combusturi eandem igni dicuntur. cap. xvii. 16. Distinctius autem capite sequente xviii. ejus judicium exponitur. Etenim primò v. 1. 2. 3. annunciatur ejus casus, Angelo celsa voce præconiante: Cecidit, cecidit Babylon illa magna, & facta est domicilium Dæmonum, & custodia omnis Spiritus impuri, & custodia omnis avis impuræ & exosæ. Quo casu vulgato, v. 4. Vox ex cœlo clamat: Exite ex ea, popule mi, & peccatorum ejus participes ne sitis, ne participes etiam plagarum ejus reddamini. Cumque casu eo susque deque habito nil de fastu suo remitteret, quin potius in corde suo diceret: Regina sedeo, & vidua non ero, & luctum non videbo: Deus v. 6. 7. jubet illi reddere pro merito, διπλῶσαι αὐτῇ διπλᾶ ὅσα ἐποίησεν, ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασεν κεράσατε αὐτῇ διπλοῦν, duplicare ei duplum, secundum opera ejus, in poculo, quod propinavit, propinare ei duplum, & quantum se glorificavit, & luxuriata est, tantum ei dare cruciatum & luctum. Unde consequitur posterior, idemque ultimus & peremtorius ejus casus. v. 8. Propterea una hora venient plagæ ejus, mors & luctus & pestilentia. Et cremabitur igni, quia fortis est Dominus Deus, qui illam judicat. Quem casum acerbè deplorantes Reges terræ, qui cum ea fcortati sunt, & mercatores, qui ex ea quæstum antehac fecerant, deincéps tragicè inducuntur.
units.tr: XII. Finally, the judgment of great Babylon proceeds by stages. The ten horns of the beast on which the woman sits, that is, ten kings who will first hate the harlot and forsake her, so that she is naked; second, will devour her flesh; third, will burn her with fire, are said to do so. cap. xvii. 16. Her judgment is set out more distinctly in the following chapter, xviii. For first, vv. 1-3, her fall is announced, an angel proclaiming with a loud voice: "Fallen, fallen is that great Babylon, and has become a habitation of demons, and a prison of every unclean spirit, and a prison of every unclean and hated bird." When this fall has been published, v. 4, a voice from heaven cries: "Come out of her, my people, and do not share in her sins, lest you receive also a share in her plagues." But since she, treating this fall lightly, did not give up her pride, but rather said in her heart, "I sit a queen, and I shall not be a widow, and I shall not see mourning," God, vv. 6-7, commands that she be repaid according to her deeds: "double to her double [διπλῶσαι αὐτῇ διπλᾶ], according to her works; in the cup which she mixed, mix for her double; and as much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much give her torment and mourning." From this follows her second and last, and decisive, fall, v. 8: "Therefore her plagues will come in one hour, death and mourning and pestilence; and she will be burned with fire, for the Lord God who judges her is strong." The kings of the earth who committed fornication with her, and the merchants who had made gain from her before, are henceforth introduced mourning this fall tragically.

units.la: Iudicium ejusdem per gradus procedens.
units.tr: The same judgment, proceeding by stages.

units.la: XIII. Hæc de Babylone magna in universum Apocalypsis commemorat. Ex quibus in promptu est ejus definitionem quandam ὡς (ςυλλήβδην) omnia complexam, cudere; quæ ejusmodi esse potest: Babylon magna est mystica mater fcortationum, & abominationum terræ, quæ gravissimorum scelerum, fornicationis, seductionis ad eandem horribilis, tyrannidis notoriæ, blasphemiarum, superbiæ intolerandæ, incantationum & nundinationis exquisitæ notis insignita, super aquis multis, & bestia ipsa coccinea septem capita, seu totidem montes, quibus incubat, & decem cornua, seu totidem Reges potestatem suam ei largientes, habente, gloriosissimæ Reginæ poculum aureum plenum abominationis & immunditiæ fcortationis manu sua gestantis instar, sedens fornicari cum Regibus terræ, & infanda quæque patrare non definit, donec Deo illam judicante, & Regibus odio habentibus cadat, existens domicilium Dæmonum, & custodia Spiritus impuri, avisque immundæ & exosæ omnis, deserenda & deserta à piis omnibus; & ne sic quidem immanium scelerum pœnitudine ulla ducta, imò exasperata, & magis etiam se proferens, peremtorio ultimoque casu prolapsa, & cumulatis unà horâ ejus plagis, denique igni cremata funditus horribilitérque pereat.
units.tr: XIII. These are the things the Apocalypse recounts about great Babylon in general. From them it is easy to coin a single definition that embraces all of them in brief (ὡς συλλήβδην): "Great Babylon is the mystical mother of fornications and abominations of the earth, marked by the signs of the gravest crimes: fornication, horrible seduction to the same, notorious tyranny, blasphemies, intolerable pride, and exquisite sorcery and trafficking; sitting upon many waters and upon the scarlet beast itself, which has seven heads, that is as many mountains on which she sits, and ten horns, that is as many kings granting their power to her; holding in her hand, like a most glorious queen, a golden cup full of the abomination and filth of her fornication; sitting and fornicating with the kings of the earth, and not ceasing to commit every unspeakable deed until God judges her and the kings who hate her bring her down. She becomes a habitation of demons, a watchhouse of every unclean spirit and of every unclean and hated bird, to be deserted and abandoned by all the pious. Yet not even so does she repent of her monstrous crimes, but is rather exasperated and displays herself all the more; she falls in a decisive and final fall, and with her plagues heaped upon her in one hour, at last she is burned with fire and perishes utterly and horribly."

units.la: XIV. Infaustas dirásque mulieres quasdam gentilium mythologi poëmatis suis exagitárunt. Aten, fictitiam Divam quandam πάντας ἀάνη omnes infestare, nocere omnibus, Homerus Iliad. 1. finxit. Pandora, prima mulier, à Vulcano Jovis jussu, si Hesiodo fides est, fabricata, cum pixide clausa Jovis, ejusdem jussu ad Epimetheum, quòd ignem è Cœlo furatus in terram detulisset, missa, cujus aperta pixide omne malorum genus, morbi & calamitates sævissimæ orbem terrarum impleverunt. Circe, Solis & Perses Nymphæ, nec non Orphei filia, Veneficiorum mater, Ulyffis socios ob intemperantiam propinato poculo suo in porcos canésque commutavit. Monstra multa in orbe generata initio φλιτϛ fui adversus Vigilantium Hieronymus recitat. Quæ verò demum inauspicata mulier, quod monstrum horribile est, quod cum Babylone magna, matre scortationum & abominationum omnium paria facere possit? De qua verius quàm de Harpyis, Virgiliana illa ex Æneid. lib. 1. enunciaveris: Triftius haud illa monstrum, nec sævior ulla Pestis, & ira Deúm stygiis sese extulit undis.
units.tr: XIV. The poets of the pagan mythologists have harried certain ill-omened and dreadful women. Homer, in Iliad 1, invented a fictitious goddess, Ate, who harms all men [πάντας ἀάνη]. Pandora, the first woman, was fashioned by Vulcan at Jove's command, if Hesiod is to be trusted, and sent with a closed box from Jove, by his order, to Epimetheus, because Prometheus had stolen fire from heaven and brought it down to earth. When the box was opened, every kind of evil, diseases and most savage calamities, filled the world. Circe, daughter of the Sun and the Nymph Perse, and also a daughter of Orpheus, mother of sorcery, changed Ulysses' companions into pigs and dogs with a poisoned cup, because of their intemperance. Jerome, writing against Vigilantius, recounts many monsters born in the world from the beginning [φλιτϛ]. But what unlucky woman, what monstrous creature, could be compared with Babylon the Great, the mother of harlotries and of all abominations? Of her, far more truly than of the Harpies, you could say those lines of Virgil from Aeneid 1: "Nor did any monster more sad or pestilence more savage, nor any wrath of the gods, rise up from the Stygian waves."

units.la: XV. Eccui enim non stent comæ, cogitanti mulierem, ex eo scil. sexu, qui viso etiam mure trepidare solet, bestiam adeò immanem non reformidantem, sed audacter illam concendentem, agitantem, regentem, Reges terrarum subigentem, sanguine sanctorum ad temulentiam usque turgentem? Quid hic Spiritus Dei aliud indigitare voluit, quàm infernalibus furiis instinctam agitatámque fuisse mulierem isthanc, quæ mulieri illi sanctæ, masculum parienti & in desertum fugienti Apoc. xii. v. 6. tremendam adeò terribilémque se se præbere voluit.
units.tr: XV. Who would not have his hair stand on end, thinking of a woman, of that sex which is wont to tremble even at the sight of a mouse, who is not afraid of so huge a beast, but boldly mounts it, drives it, rules it, subdues the kings of the earth, and swells with the blood of the saints to drunkenness? What did the Spirit of God wish to indicate here, except that this woman was driven and goaded by infernal furies, whom He wished to show as terrible and dreadful to that holy woman who bore a male child and fled into the wilderness, Rev. 12:6?

units.la: XVI. Cùm verò Babylon illa magna in fronte sua habeat nomen μυςήριον Mysterium, adeóque ex eorum genere sit, quæ Scriptura ænigmata, non quæ ἀινιγμα seu sermonem clarum Habac. ii. 6. vocat; opera certè non mediocriter danda est, ut ænigma illud feliciter extricetur, & extricatum ad spiritalem usum, permagnum certè, accommodetur. Inprasentiarum autem μυςηριωδεις, falsas mysterii hujus interpretationes, seu potius ςπιϛλώσεις detorsiones quasdam, quas olim nonnulli animo certè innocentiore, hodie verò non pauci, quibus malè sibi conscii cor palpitat, nocentiore longè excogitarunt, acriterque pertendendo propugnant, ad sanioris hermeneuticeS limam revocare nobis constitutum est.
