The order is divided into three classes: priests and chaplains, who perform the sacred offices and try to obtain by prayer, reading and singing every blessing and happiness for their lords who fight; knights, all of noble birth, who recite only the Lord's Prayer a fixed number of times and rule the order from then on; and servants, who are bound to carry out the commands of the knights. After they had fought vigorously in Syria for almost three hundred years, in 1300 they were driven from there by the captain of the Damascenes, and they then took the island of Rhodes by storm. There, according to eight tongues, or nations, namely French, Auvergnat, Western Frankish, Italian, Spanish, Aragonese, English and German, and Castilian Spanish, they created as many Masters or Priors, subject to one Prince, and besides these, in the Christian provinces, others also everywhere, placed over the commanderies of the orders in their provinces. Then in 1523, lacking help and driven out by discordant princes, they occupied the island of Malta in 1529, and they still defend it vigorously; they are more praiseworthy than the other monks, if you except their superstition, in that they do not rage, as the others do, against the bowels of Christ but against those of barbarians and infidels, and so defend the whole Christian world. But enough about these.

units.la: LXXVI. Atque ex his Hierarchiæ, seu Cleri Romani dominantis Civitas Religiosa longè maxima & amplissima, potentissima, Sole meridiano clariùs conspicitur. Dominantur in ea מלך ושרים Rex & Principes, puta Impera-
units.tr: LXXVI. From these facts it is seen, clearer than noonday sun, that the religious city of the ruling Hierarchy, that is, of the Roman clergy, is by far the largest, most extensive and most powerful. In it rule King and Princes [מלך ושרים], namely the Emperor

units.la: tor ille Scenicus, Papa, ejúsque facerimi Principes, Cardinales puta, Regibus adæquati, Curiales Romani Patriarchæ Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, Præpositi, Archipresbyteri, Archidiaconi, Vicarii, Archimandritæ, Abbates unà cum עברי מושלים servis dominantium, hoc est, dominationis ejus instrumentis, Sacrificulis, Presbyteris, Doctoribus, Theologis, Canonistis, Canonicis, Diaconis, Subdiaconis, Acoluthis, Exorcistis, Lectoribus, Ostiariis, Monachorum infinitis cohortibus, Jesuitis, Fratribus, Equitibus: Militibus Religiosis, iisque omnibus tanto numero, ut iniri is vix ab ullo mortalium queat. Dominantur illi non uni Nationi, Provinciæ. Dominantur Imperatori, dominantur Regibus, Principibus Christiani Orbis. Ante Reformationem annorum plus quingentorum intervallo dominati sunt conscientiis, fortunis orbis Christiani universi. Cedo mihi Civitatem Religiosam dominantem ejusmodi aliam inde à temporibus S. Johannis, cui Babylon Civitas illa Magna in visione oblata est! Quòd si alia vel dominans, vel magis dominans demonstrari nequit (uti sanè æternum nequit) hæc, hæc, non alia Magna illa Civitas Babylonica & Hierarchia, seu Clerus Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominans, cæteris paribus, Magna illa Babylon esse manifestè convincitur.
units.tr: that theatrical emperor, the Pope, and his most sacred Princes, namely the Cardinals, who are equal to kings; the Roman courtiers, the Patriarchs, Archbishops, Bishops, Provosts, Archpriests, Archdeacons, Vicars and Archimandrites, and Abbots, together with the servants of the rulers [עברי מושלים], that is, the instruments of his domination: priests, presbyters, teachers, theologians, canonists, canons, deacons, subdeacons, acolytes, exorcists, lectors, doorkeepers, countless troops of monks, Jesuits, friars, and knights, religious soldiers, and all of them in such numbers that scarcely any mortal can count them. They rule not over one nation or one province. They rule over the Emperor, they rule over kings and princes of the Christian world. For more than five hundred years before the Reformation they held dominion over the consciences and fortunes of the whole Christian world. Show me another religious city ruling in this way since the time of St John, to whom that great city Babylon was shown in vision! But if no other city, either ruling or ruling more, can be pointed out (as indeed it never can be), then this one, this and no other, is manifestly proven, other things being equal, to be that great Babylon: the Hierarchy, or the ruling clergy of the Roman Church.

units.la: DISSERTATIONIS VIII.
units.tr: DISSERTATION VIII.

units.la: SECTIO SECUNDA, QUA
units.tr: SECOND SECTION, IN WHICH

units.la: Hierarchiæ, seu Clero Romano dominanti subesse Populum Magnum, qui Bestiæ nomine venit, demonstratur.
units.tr: It is shown that the people which is called by the name of the Beast is subject to the Roman Hierarchy, or Clergy, that rules.

units.la: BREVIARIUM.
units.tr: SUMMARY.

units.la: I. Civitas Magna subditis non caret. Babylonis M. subditi sunt Bestiæ, Populus magnus. II. Hierarchiæ Romanæ subditam esse Bestiam septicipitem, Syllogismo generali demonstratur. Propositionis nexus. III. Assumtio per singulas partes probatur. Bestia hominem animalem, & latè patens Imperium stylo Scripturæ significat. IV. Atqui Hierarchiæ R. subest Imperium latissimè patens, Romanum, quâ Pseudo-Christianum, V. quod, ceu animale merito cum Bestia comparatur. VI. Bestia quo sensu fuerit, non sit, ascensura ex abysso & in interitum itura sit? VII. Imperio Romano Pseudo-Christiano, à Dracone seu Imperio Romano Ethnico thronum & potestatem accipienti, id competere, probatur. VIII. Imago ejusdem in veteri Israële carnali ostenditur.
units.tr: I. A great city is not without subjects. The subjects of the great Babylon are the Beast, the great people. II. That the seven-headed Beast is subject to the Roman Hierarchy is demonstrated by a general syllogism. The connection of the premise. III. The assumption is proved part by part. In the style of Scripture the Beast signifies a rational-animal man and a widely extended empire. IV. But the Roman Hierarchy is subject to an empire of very wide extent, the Roman, as it is Pseudo-Christian, V. which, being an animal, is rightly compared with the Beast. VI. In what sense the Beast was, is not, is to ascend out of the abyss and is to go into perdition. VII. It is proved that this belongs to the Pseudo-Christian Roman Empire, which receives its throne and power from the Dragon, that is, the heathen Roman Empire. VIII. The image of the same is shown in the carnal Israel of old.

units.la: IX. Duo genera hominum, Bestiam admirantium, & nul-lo loco habentium.
units.tr: IX. Two kinds of men, those who admire the Beast and those who count for nothing.

units.la: X. Eadem genera Imperio Romano Christiano conve-niunt.
units.tr: X. The same two kinds belong to the Christian Roman Empire.

units.la: XI. Bestiae habitus externus coccineus, eidem Imperio aptatur.
units.tr: XI. The scarlet outward appearance of the Beast is fitted to the same Empire.

units.la: XII. Os Bestiae in blasphemias diductum.
units.tr: XII. The mouth of the Beast opened to blasphemies.

units.la: XIII. Imperii Romani Pseudo-Christiani blasphemiae.
units.tr: XIII. The blasphemies of the Pseudo-Christian Roman Empire.

units.la: XIV. Bestiae capita septem, totidemque montes & Reges tribuuntur.
units.tr: XIV. The seven heads of the Beast, and as many mountains and kings, are ascribed to it.

units.la: XV. Roma septimontia est; sub Constantino M. in certas dynastias, seu Provinciarum capita distributa; ejúsque Imperio statim sub eodem Constantino hypocritae, homines animales multi se sociarunt.
units.tr: XV. Rome is a city of seven hills; under Constantine the Great it was divided into certain dynasties, or capitals of provinces; and immediately under this same Constantine many hypocrites, many rational-animal men, joined themselves to its empire.

units.la: XVI. Montes septem Romae, quā tales, & quā monimentum totidem dynastiarum, Regúmque seu Rectorum earum competunt.
units.tr: XVI. The seven hills of Rome, both as hills and as a monument of as many dynasties and their kings or rulers, belong to it.

units.la: XVII. Septem montes illos mulier seu Hierarchia Ecclesiae Romanae sub Phoca Imperatore insedit.
units.tr: XVII. The woman, that is, the Hierarchy of the Roman Church, sat upon those seven hills under the Emperor Phocas.

units.la: XVIII. Quinque Reges ceciderunt, unus fuit, alius nondum venit, Octavus ex septem oriturus. Impletum id per incursiones barbarorum populorum, stans Imperium Graecum, Regnum Italicum & Germanicum in Occidente superventurum.
units.tr: XVIII. Five kings have fallen, one is, another has not yet come, an eighth, who is of the seven, is to arise. This was fulfilled through the invasions of barbarian peoples; the standing Greek Empire, the Italian and German Kingdom, is to come upon the West.

units.la: XIX. Bestiae cornua decem Reges sunt.
units.tr: XIX. The ten horns of the Beast are ten kings.

units.la: XX. Prophetiae & complementi ordo.
units.tr: XX. The order of the prophecy and its fulfilment.

units.la: XXI. Pugna cornuum cum Agno, Reformationis tempore maximè.
units.tr: XXI. The war of the horns against the Lamb, especially at the time of the Reformation.

units.la: XXII. Cornua seu Reges decem, Papae Vasalli, ex Hildebrando aliisque enumerati.
units.tr: XXII. The horns, or the ten kings, vassals of the Pope, enumerated from Hildebrand and others.

units.la: XXIII. Reges decem qui Reformationis tempore cum Bestia pro Hierarchia Ecclesiae Romanae adversus Christum unicum Ecclesiae Caput decertárunt.
units.tr: XXIII. The ten kings who at the time of the Reformation fought with the Beast for the Roman Church's Hierarchy against Christ, the one Head of the Church.

units.la: XXIV. Bestiæ & cornuum conflictus cum Sanctis, & cum Agno distinguitur. XXV. Reges ab Agno vincuntur. XXVI. Argumentum concluditur.
units.tr: XXIV. The conflict of the Beast and the horns with the saints, and with the Lamb, is distinguished. XXV. The kings are conquered by the Lamb. XXVI. The argument is concluded.

units.la: I. Civitatem Magnam Babylonicam esse Hierarchiam, seu Clerum Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominantem abundè demonstravimus. Cæterùm Civitas magna dominans subditis destitui non potest. Cessat enim dominium, ubi subjectio, servitus nulla est. Hinc adeo Spiritus Dei Babyloni Magnæ subditos, Bestiam, quæ Meretricem portat, septem capitibus constantem, in septem collibus habitantem, & decem cornuum, seu Regum totidem potentia suffultum Apoc. xvii. 3. 7. 8-18. tribuit. Esse autem Bestiam hancce Populum magnum animalem, seu multitudinem hominum, Christi nomen oretenus confitentium, at de cætero non tam Christo Domino, quàm Clero dominanti, seu Civitati magnæ parentium, quæ post Romam Ethnicam ad Christum conversam habeat septem capita, seu totidem Provincias Rectoribus suis obnoxias, & loco certo septem montibus superstructo adstringi velit; denique sub septimo capite seu octavo Rege habeat cornua decem, totidemque Reges, cum Rege illo octavo conspirantes, & ad tempus Agnum, Christum, fideles & electos, oppugnantes, donec ab Agno victi odium internecinum adversus Meretricem concipiant, & ejusdem finali excidio illud denique expleant; superius Dissert. iij. 32-40. liquidò comprobavimus.
units.tr: I. We have abundantly shown that the great Babylon is the Hierarchy, or the Clergy of the Roman Church that rules. Moreover, a great ruling city cannot be without subjects, for where there is no subjection or servitude, there is no dominion. Hence the Spirit of God ascribes to the great Babylon, as its subjects, the Beast that carries the Harlot, consisting of seven heads, dwelling on seven hills, and supported by the power of ten horns, or as many kings (Rev. 17:3, 7, 8–18). Now, we have clearly demonstrated above (Dissert. iii. 32–40) that this Beast is a great rational-animal people, or a multitude of men who confess the name of Christ with their mouths but otherwise are not so much subject to Christ the Lord as to the ruling Clergy, that is, that they are obedient to the great city that is the parent of them; that after heathen Rome was converted to Christ it has seven heads, or as many provinces subject to their rulers, and wishes to be bound to a certain place built on seven mountains; finally, that under the seventh head, or eighth king, it has ten horns, and as many kings conspiring with that eighth king, who for a time fight against the Lamb, Christ, the faithful and the elect, until, conquered by the Lamb, they conceive a deadly hatred against the Harlot and at last fulfil her utter destruction.

units.la: II. Quòd si igitur Hierarchiam seu Clerum Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominantem subditum habere ejusmodi populum, qui Bestiæ Babyloni Magnæ parentis numeros omnes impleat, ampliùs, cæteris paribus, cum Babylonem Magnam esse, constabit. Atqui habere, Syllogismo sequenti demonstramus:
units.tr: II. If, therefore, the Hierarchy or the ruling Clergy of the Roman Church has such a people as its subjects, one that fills all the numbers of the Beast of the great mother Babylon, then, other things being equal, it will be established that it is the great Babylon. Now we prove that it has such a people by the following syllogism:

units.la: Quicunque cœtus subditum sibi habet Imperium Romanum Pseudo-Christianum, à Romano Ethnico ortum, Israëli carnali haud absimile, per sanguinis Christi professionem coloratum, & sanguinis Sanctorum, blasphemiarúmque reum; sub Imperatore Constantino M. septem dynastiis, totidémque rectoribus distinctum; quarum quinque post Phocam ceciderunt, una, Imperium Græcum stetit, supervenientibus in occidente Regno Italico & Germanico, quod decem Regibus sociatis pro Papa adversus Christum unicum Ecclesiæ Caput decertavit, & ab eodem denique victum est: Ille subditam sibi habet Bestiam, quæ fuit, non est, ex abysso ascendit, in interitum ibit, coccinea est, plena nominibus blasphemiæ, septem capita, montes seu Reges habet, quorum quinque ceciderunt, alius est, alius nondum venit; superveniente octavo, qui ex septem est, & decem cornua habet una cum Bestia cum Agno belligerantia; & ab eodem vincenda; adeòque cæteris paribus, est Babylon Magna.
units.tr: Whatever assembly has as its subject the Pseudo-Christian Roman Empire, which arose from the heathen Roman, not unlike carnal Israel, coloured by the profession of the blood of Christ, and guilty of the blood of the saints and of blasphemies, and which under the Emperor Constantine the Great was divided into seven dynasties and as many rulers, of which five fell after Phocas, one, the Greek Empire, stood, the Italian Kingdom and then the German coming upon the West, which, with ten kings allied to it, fought for the Pope against Christ, the one Head of the Church, and was at last conquered by him: that assembly has as its subject a Beast which was, is not, ascends out of the abyss, goes to perdition, is scarlet, full of names of blasphemy, has seven heads, mountains or kings, of which five have fallen, one is, another has not yet come; when the eighth comes, who is of the seven, it has ten horns, which fight with the Lamb together with the Beast, and it is to be conquered by him; and therefore, other things being equal, it is the great Babylon.

units.la: Atqui Hierarchia, seu Clerus Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominans subditum sibi habet Imperium Romanum PseudoChristianum, à Romano Ethnico ortum, Israëli carnali haud absimile, per sanguinis Christi professionem coloratum, & sanguinis sanctorum, blasphemiarúmque reum, sub Imperatore Constantino M. septem dynastiis, totidemque Rectoribus distinctum, quorum quinque post Phocam ceciderunt, una, Imperium Græcum stetit, supervenientibus Regno Italico & mox Germanico, quod decem Regibus sociatis pro Papa adversus Christum unicum Ecclesiæ caput decertavit, & ab eodem denique victum est.
units.tr: But the Hierarchy, or the ruling Clergy of the Roman Church, has as its subject the Pseudo-Christian Roman Empire, which arose from the heathen Roman, not unlike carnal Israel, coloured by the profession of the blood of Christ, and guilty of the blood of the saints and of blasphemies, divided under the Emperor Constantine the Great into seven dynasties and as many rulers, of which five fell after Phocas, one, the Greek Empire, stood, the Italian Kingdom and soon the German coming upon it, which with ten allied kings fought for the Pope against Christ, the one Head of the Church, and was at last conquered by him.

units.la: Ergo Hierarchia seu Clerus Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominans subditam sibi habet Bestiam, quæ fuit, non est, ex abyssο ascendit, in interitum ibit, coccinea est, plena nominibus blasphemiæ, septem capita, montes seu Reges habet, quorum quinque ceciderunt, unus est, alius nondum venit, superveniente octavo, qui ex septem est, & decem cornua habet, una cum Bestia cum Agno belligerantia, & ab eodem vincenda; adeóque cæteris paribus, Babylon Magna est.
units.tr: Therefore the Hierarchy, or the ruling Clergy of the Roman Church, has as its subject the Beast, which was, is not, ascends out of the abyss, goes to perdition, is scarlet, full of names of blasphemy, has seven heads, mountains or kings, of which five have fallen, one is, another has not yet come; when the eighth comes, who is of the seven, it has ten horns, which fight with the Lamb together with the Beast, and it is to be conquered by him; and therefore, other things being equal, it is the great Babylon.

units.la: Propositionis nexus arctissimus est, quippe definiti & definitionis identitate nixus. Bestia enim, qualem Propositio Prophetiæ ipsius verbis describit, Imperium Romanum Pseudo-Christianum, quale eadem Propositio describit, definitur, uti verborum Prophetiæ, & eventus harmonia docet, id quod partim Differt. iij. 32-40. demonstravimus, partim procedente tractatione Σ. Θ. ampliùs demonstraturi sumus.
units.tr: The connection of the premise is very close, being founded on the identity of the thing defined and the definition. For the Beast, such as the premise describes in the very words of the prophecy, is defined as the Pseudo-Christian Roman Empire, such as the same premise describes it; as the words of the prophecy and the harmony of the events teach. We have partly demonstrated this in Dissert. iii. 32–40, and partly we shall demonstrate it further as the treatment proceeds, in Σ and Θ.

units.la: III. Assumtionem quoad singulas partes probatum imus. Etenim Primò Babyloni Magnæ, Civitati Magnæ, Meretrici Apoc. xvii. 3. 7. 8. tribuitur θηρίον Bestia, eandem portans, adeóque eidem subdita, super qua Mulier ceu dominans rectrix, sedet. Cum Bestia S. literæ Psalm. xlix. 21. lxxiii. 2. Eccl. iii. 18. 2 Pet. ii. 12. Jud. verf. 10. hominem imagine & Spiritu Dei destitutum, adeóque ψυχικὸν seu ἀνθρώπινον animalem comparat. Quò pertinent ארבע חיות רבות quatuor bestiæ grandes è mari ascendentes, quas Daniel cap. vii. 3. vidit. Inter eas verf. 7. quarta דחילא ואמתני ותקיפא יתירא formidolosa, terribilis, & fortis valde, haud dubiè Imperium Romanum tum Ethnicum, tum Christianum significat. Bestiam illam, quæ Babylonicam meretricem portat, Imperium Romanum non Ethnicum, sed Christianum seu Christi nomen professum notare Differt. iij. 20-27. clarè satis comprobavi.
units.tr: III. We go through the assumption as to its individual parts. First, the Beast is attributed to the great Babylon, the great city, the Harlot (Rev. 17:3, 7, 8), a θηρίον [beast], carrying her and therefore subject to her, upon which the Woman sits as ruling mistress. Holy Scripture likens the Beast to a man deprived of the image and Spirit of God, and therefore to a rational-animal man [ψυχικὸν, or ἀνθρώπινον], (Ps. 49:21; 73:2; Eccl. 3:18; 2 Pet. 2:12; Jude v. 10). To this belong the "four great beasts" [ארבע חיות רבות] coming up from the sea, which Daniel saw (Dan. 7:3). Among them, in v. 7, the fourth, "terrible, dreadful, and exceedingly strong" [dechila ve-amtani ve-taqifa yatira], undoubtedly signifies the Roman Empire, both heathen and Christian. I have sufficiently shown, in Dissert. iii. 20–27, that the Beast that carries the Babylonian harlot signifies the Roman Empire not as heathen but as Christian, that is, one that professes the name of Christ.

units.la: IV. An
units.tr: IV. Whether

units.la: IV. An igitur probatione ampliore rem indigere putabimus? Numquid enim non Hierarchiæ, seu Clero Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominanti Imperium Romanum Christianum aliquando universum, atque etiamnum majore sui parte in spiritualibus & temporalibus paruit, parétque? Quomodo, quibus temporum periodis, quibus denique machinationibus sibi Imperium illud Pontifices Romani subjugaverint, adeóque Imperatorem, Reges, Principesque Vasallos & feudatarios suos effecerint, Historia Patus, Periodum Ecclesiæ Romanæ quartam, quintam & sextam enarrans, καὶ λεπίν edisseruit. Proxima etiam Sectio, imperiúmque quod Romanus Pontifex in Orbem Christianum universum sibi vendicat & gestit hactenus, geritque, tradet.
units.tr: IV. Whether, then, we shall think the matter needs fuller proof? For did not the Roman Empire, once wholly Christian and still for the greater part of it, obey and still obey the Hierarchy, that is, the Clergy of the Roman Church in which dominion lies, both in spiritual and in temporal matters? How the Roman Pontiffs subjected that Empire to themselves, in what periods of time and by what machinations they made the Emperor, the Kings, the Princes and the Nobles their vassals and feudatories, the history of the Papacy has set forth minutely, narrating the fourth, fifth and sixth periods of the Roman Church. The next section will also set out the dominion which the Roman Pontiff claims for himself over the whole Christian world, and has hitherto sought and still seeks.

units.la: V. Imperium Romanum primò fuit Ethnicum, mox verò Christianum, Constantini M. auspiciis, licet jam tum permixtum hominibus hypocritis & animalibus, qui Christum ore quidem professi, pilum, non animum mutárunt, ex quibus tot hæretici sati sunt: tandem Christianum ψευδωνύμως, quando Clero Romano dominanti succubuit, ejus in spiritualibus & temporalibus potestatem supremam agnovit, sedem Romanam ceu fidei & mysteriorum omnium magistram & dominam respexit, modum & colendi Dei, & regendorum hominum ab eadem ceu ὠνπεγπεμκῶς, & ex plenitudine quadam potestatis, dominante recepit, & ex Imperante serviens reddita, non tam verè Imperium, utpote in Pontifices translatum mansit, quàm clientum & Vasallorum Pontificis, Imperatoris scilicet sui novi, evaserunt, quodcunque nomen præ se tulerint. Atqueisthoc qui in se, temporum calamitate, & tremendo quodam Dei judicio, admiserunt, non utique spiritu Dei agitati, sed suis ratiociniis, & consiliis carnalibus moti in se id admiserunt, & eadem ratione se populum magnum animainimalem non tam divina, quàm humana authoritate fretum, eligentem id dicere & facere, non quod Spiritus Dei in Verbo præscripsit, sed quod Ecclesia, hoc est, Papa, Clerus dominans dicendum faciendúmque præscripsit; adeóque humanum nomen, humanas erroneásque opiniones sequentem prodidit. Quod dictum velim citra ullam injuriam eorum, qui vel olim, postquam Clerus Romanus Imperium, Populúmque tantum sibi subjecit, in ditione licet habitantes ea, quam Clerus sibi subjecit, Christo Domino Ecclesiæ unico intemeratam fidem servaverunt; vel hodiéque intemeratam servant. Quos cùm solus Deus compertos habuerit, habeátque, nos de personis judicium nobis arrogamus nulli, Deo committentes servos suos, cui soli Domino stantque, cadúntque. Ad animum hëic revocari velim ea, quæ Differt. iv. 3. 4. &c. cam in rem copiosíus dicta sunt.
units.tr: V. The Roman Empire was first pagan, but afterwards Christian, under the auspices of Constantine the Great, although even then it was mixed with hypocrites and carnal men, who professed Christ with their mouths but changed their coat, not their heart, and from whom so many heretics have arisen. Finally it became Christian in name only, when it submitted to the dominant Roman Clergy, acknowledged the Clergy's supreme power in spiritual and temporal matters, looked upon the Roman See as the teacher and mistress of faith and of all mysteries, and received from it, as a kind of supreme authority and from a certain fullness of power, the manner of worshipping God and of governing men. Having been turned from ruler into servant, it remained not truly an empire, since it had been transferred to the Pontiffs, but its people became the clients and vassals of the Pontiff, that is, of their new Emperor, whatever name they bore. Those who admitted this into themselves, in the calamity of the times and by a certain dreadful judgment of God, were not moved by the Spirit of God, but by their own reasonings and carnal counsels they admitted it into themselves; and by the same reasoning they made a great and animal people, relying not so much on divine as on human authority, choose to say and do not what the Spirit of God has prescribed in the Word, but what the Church, that is, the Pope and the dominant Clergy, has prescribed to be said and done. Thus they revealed that they follow human names and human and erroneous opinions. I would wish this said without any injury to those who, either formerly, after the Roman Clergy had subjected to itself the Empire and the people, living within the realm which the Clergy had subjected to itself, kept the faith inviolate toward Christ the Lord, the sole head of the Church; or who even today keep it inviolate. Since God alone has known and knows them, we do not arrogate to ourselves any judgment about persons, committing his servants to God, to whom alone they stand or fall. I would wish these matters to be recalled to mind, which were spoken more fully on this subject in Dissert. iv. 3, 4, etc.

units.la: VI. Quæ porro Bestiæ Babyloni parenti, Spiritus Dei, ratione ortus & interitus, habitus externi, oris, capitum & cornuum tribuit, eadem populo, qui sub Cleri Romani dominantis jugum missus est, competere, probandum nunc etiam fuerit. Bestiæ igitur primò ortus & interitus sic Apoc. xvii. 8. describitur: Bestia quam vidisti, fuit, & non est, etiamsi est, & ascensura est ex abysso, & in perditionem itura. Ante omnia imago quædam seu Civitas & Respublica præterita indigetatur, cum qua partim convenit, partim non convenit. Imaginem illam esse vel Draconis, seu Diaboli, populo Romano persecutore induti, qui thronum & potestatem suam Bestiæ cessisse Apoc. xiii. 2. dicitur, vel Israëlis carnalis veteris Differt. iv. 32. 33. ostendimus. Fuit igitur Bestia hæc sive in Dracone, ratione ejusdem potestatis & throni, secundum quam imago fuit Bestiæ: sive in carnali Israële, qui circumcisus, populi Dei nomine insignitus, in cultus Divini exercitio sedentibus Bestia quæ sensu fuerit, non sit, ascensura ex abysso & in interitum itura sit? tibus in loco, quem Deus elegerat, subjectus fuit. Non est quatenus populus ille magnus similis licet vel Draconi, vel Israëli illi carnali, nec Draco tamen est, qui gentes ad crassam idololatriam seduxit, cùm populus ille crassam idololatriam deseruit; nec carnalis ille Israël, jure scilicet, quia in N. T. status ille & politia Ecclesiæ non obtinet amplius, quæ in V. T. obtinuit, neque Ecclesia Christiana vel Dominis religiosis, vel certo loco affixa amplius est. Etiamsi est, similis scilicet eatenus & Draconi & Israëli carnali. Et ascensura est ex abyssο, hoc est, ex multitudine gentium, si Draconis typus spectetur, vel alia omni, quàm Cœlesti origine, si Israëlis carnalis typus valeat, utpote quæ (Bestia) non utique Divina origine & institutione nitetur, cùm Deus ejusmodi Ecclesiam, cujus caput terrestre fit, & quæ certam fixámque sedem in mundo eligit, ut ab ea jus & fas omne arceßat, non instituerit, sed aliunde caput suum proferet. Et in perditionem itura, cùm in religione præsertim stabile nihil sit, quod Deum authorem non habet, & plantatio omnis, quam Cœlestis ille Pater non plantavit, eradicari debeat, Matth. xv. 13.
units.tr: VI. It must now also be proved that what the Spirit of God ascribes to the Beast of Babylon, its parent, in respect of its origin and end, its external appearance, its mouth, heads and horns, applies to the people which has been placed under the yoke of the dominant Roman Clergy. First, then, the origin and end of the Beast is described thus in Rev. xvii. 8: The beast that you saw was, and is not, and yet is, and is about to ascend out of the abyss and go to perdition. Above all, a certain image or past city and commonwealth is to be sought, with which the present one partly agrees and partly does not. That the image is either of the Dragon, or of the Devil, who was clothed in the Roman people as persecutor, and who is said in Rev. xiii. 2 to have given his throne and power to the Beast, or of the carnal Israel of old, we have shown in Dissert. iv. 32, 33. The Beast, therefore, was, either in the Dragon, in respect of the same power and throne according to which the image was of the Beast, or in carnal Israel, which, circumcised and marked with the name of the people of God, was subject to those who sat in the exercise of divine worship in the place God had chosen. Is not, in so far as that great people, though similar either to the Dragon or to that carnal Israel, is not the Dragon, which led the nations into gross idolatry, since that people has abandoned gross idolatry; nor is it that carnal Israel, namely by right, because in the New Testament that state and polity of the Church no longer holds, which held in the Old Testament, nor is the Christian Church any longer bound to religious rulers or to a fixed place. Yet it is, namely similar so far to both the Dragon and carnal Israel. And is about to ascend out of the abyss, that is, out of the multitude of nations, if the type of the Dragon is considered, or out of any origin other than heavenly, if the type of carnal Israel holds, since the Beast does not rest upon divine origin and institution, since God has not instituted such a Church, whose head becomes earthly and which chooses for itself a fixed and settled seat in the world, so that it may keep away from itself all right and lawful thing; but it will put forward its head from elsewhere. And go to perdition, since in religion above all nothing is stable which has not God as its author, and every plant which the heavenly Father has not planted must be uprooted, Matt. xv. 13.

units.la: VII. Quemadmodum hæc magno illi populo, Christi nomen profeßo, & Clero Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominanti subjecto, congruant, equidem dicere nihil attinet. Rem ipsam authorem habemus. Populus ille Christianus Romano Pontifici se subjiciens, Draconi utique, Imperio Romano Ethnico potestatem ac thronum suum acceptum refert. Quem Imperatores Romani Ethnici thronum, quam potestatem eximiam habuêre, eam in se Constantinus M. transtulit, & ad posteros propagavit, donec Imperium R. Christianum primò in Spiritualibus, mox etiam in temporalibus Clero Romano subjectum, ita thronum potestatémquesuam afflixit, ut penes illud nomen & umbra, & penes Clerum dominantem res ipsa non obscurè residere coeperit. Fuit igitur Imperium R. Christianum in Dracone, quoad communem potestatem thronúmque, licet abdicatum iterum, & non est, per omnia Draconi similis, quia nec crassæ idololatriæ, uti Draco, litavit, sed desertis gentium Numinibus Christo nomen dedit, quanquam & populus ille Christianus multos hypocritas, homines animales, bestiales, uti etiam Eusebius de vita Constantini lib. iv. 54. testatur, in sinu suo retinuit, & procedente tempore in aliud idololatriæ genus collapsus est, nec thronum & potestatem reapse retinuit, sed inanibus quidem retentis, vim imperii transmisit. Tametsi est, nomine Romanum illud vetus Imperium, at reservens, & clientalaris populus. Ex abyssō verò idem ascendit, sive quia ex turba gentium magnáque multitudine populorum, Italorum, Gallorum, Hispanorum, Anglorum, Germanorum, Græcorum, Æthiopum &c. conflatum fuit, quod in se Constantinus M. recepit, Romanum Imperium, sive quia Imperium R. Christianum se progressu temporis Clero, non Divino utique consilio, sed carnalibus ratiociniis mancipavit. Sed & in interitum migraturum idem perspicuè prædictum Dan. 11. 44. 45. VII. 25. 26. reperimus.
units.tr: VII. That these things fit that great people, which professes the name of Christ and is subject to the dominant Clergy of the Roman Church, there is no need for me to say. We have the thing itself as our witness. That Christian people, submitting itself to the Roman Pontiff, undoubtedly refers its power and throne to the Dragon, that is, to the pagan Roman Empire. The throne and the remarkable power which the pagan Roman Emperors had, Constantine the Great transferred to himself and handed down to posterity, until the Christian Roman Empire, first subjected to the Roman Clergy in spiritual matters and afterwards also in temporal ones, so weakened its throne and power that the reality began not obscurely to reside with the dominant Clergy, while the name and the shadow remained with the Empire. The Christian Roman Empire, therefore, was in the Dragon, as to common power and throne, although it was again laid aside, and is not, in all respects like the Dragon, since it did not sacrifice to gross idolatry as the Dragon did, but, having abandoned the divinities of the nations, gave its name to Christ; although that Christian people also retained within its bosom many hypocrites, animal and beastly men, as Eusebius also attests in On the Life of Constantine, book iv, 54, and as time went on it fell into another kind of idolatry, nor did it in fact retain the throne and power, but, keeping the empty things, it handed over the force of empire. Yet it is, in name that ancient Roman Empire, but in the one who serves, a client and vassal people. Out of the abyss, indeed, it ascended, either because it was formed out of a crowd of nations and a great multitude of peoples, Italians, Gauls, Spaniards, English, Germans, Greeks, Ethiopians, and so on, which Constantine the Great received into himself as the Roman Empire, or because the Christian Roman Empire, as time went on, handed itself over to the Clergy, not indeed by divine counsel but by carnal reasonings. But that it will also pass into perdition the same has been plainly foretold, and we find it in Dan. xi. 44, 45; vii. 25, 26.

units.la: VIII. Neque minus Populus ille magnus Christi nom- en professus, at Clero Romano subjectus, ad amussim factus est Israëlis veteris carnalis.
units.tr: VIII. Likewise that great people, which professed the name of Christ yet was subject to the Roman clergy, was made exactly like the carnal Israel of old.

units.la: Fuit igitur etiam sic Populus ille, hoc est, imaginem quandam in veteri Republica Israëlitica conspicuam habet. Sicut enim in veteri Test. erat carnalis Israël, Pontifici & Sacerdotibus subjectus, cum iisdem certo loco cultum exercentibus communionem habens, & ab iisdem jus & fas omne repetens: ita populus ille Christi nomen professus, & Clero dominanti subjectus, Pontifici & Sacerdotibus Romanis Sacramento dixit, religionem, cultúmque omnem certo loco, Romæ scilicet, ubi Papa & Senatus Sacerdotum purpureus residet, ad-
units.tr: That people therefore also existed in this way, that is, it has a certain image visible in the old Israelite commonwealth. For just as in the Old Testament there was a carnal Israel, subject to the High Priest and the priests, holding fellowship with those who performed worship in a fixed place, and seeking from them all law and right, so that people, which professed the name of Christ and was subject to the dominant clergy, swore an oath to the Roman Pontiff and priests. It bound itself to a fixed place for religion and all worship, namely Rome, where the Pope and the purple senate of priests reside, and from there it drew its sacred rites, ceremonies and all law and right, as if from a tripod, and it still draws them today.

units.la: Imago ejusdem in veteri Israële carnali ostendunt. det, adstrinxit inde sacra, Ceremonias, jus & fas omnē velut ex tripode ac arcessivit, & hodiéque arcessit. Notis‐simum equidem est, Papatûs hyperaspistas, Bellarminum, aliósque Politiam seu Hierarchiam, & Monarchiam suam Ecclesiasticam ad modulum Hierarchiæ Israëliticæ ita effingere, ut argumento etiam ab Hierarchia illa petito Pontificiam stabilire conentur: atque eosdem insuper pertendere, communionem cum Sede Romana adeò necessariam esse, ut sine ea salutis compos reddi nemo queat. Et tamen non est, jure scilicet, quod Respublica illa Israëlis carnalis fuit. Neque enim ex Divina institutione eadem ratio Politiæ Ecclesiasticæ Israëliticæ & Christianæ est. Nusquam enim Christus vel instituit, ut in Ecclesia sit Pontificis & Sacerdotum Collegium, caput terrestre, doctores cum authoritate docentes, & legislationem & jurisdictionem exercentes, quibus propter eorum nomen, aut nescio quam successionem sit parendum; vel certam aliam sedem aut locum in mundo elegit, unde interpretatio verbi sui, aut ratio & credendi, aut leges, certúmque judicium peti debeat. Licet igitur talia facto in Populo illo Pontifici R. parente obtineant, at jure non obtinent, neque Deo, sed Pontifici, juxta vaticinium Danielis VII. 25. tempora mutanti acceptä referenda sunt. Et tamen est populus ille, hoc est, quia præ se fert nomen Christi & verbum ejus, atque in medio ejus erunt Sancti, de reliquis sperantes, quod ibidem fideles & Sancti sint (uti sanè ante Reformationem in communione illa externa Sancti, afflicti & captivi licet plures fuerunt) iccirco propter hanc spem sanctorum, & externam illorum communionem, commixtionémque, quia sic Regnum Dei in medio ipsorum erat, Ecclesia & Populus Dei vocabatur. Quomodo etiam Antichristus, licet ad Ecclesiam non pertinens, sed Bestiæ inequitans, in Ecclesia tanquam Templo Dei sedere, & ad tempus Ecclesia clesia cum Bestia in externa communione commisceri debuit. Quia vero populus ille Clero ita subjectus non est, adeóque Divinam institutionem non habet: iccirco ascendit ex abysso, institutionem suæ subjectionis & cultus omnis non à Deo, sed ab hominibus, ipso quin etiam Sathana repetit, ac propterea etiam iturus est in interitum, cùm Societatem & Rempublicam ejusmodi, quæ incunabula sua ad Deum authorem & fundatorem non refert, certa pernicies denique maneat.
units.tr: The image of this is shown in the carnal Israel of old. It is well known that the champions of the Papacy, Bellarmine and others, shape their polity or hierarchy and their ecclesiastical monarchy after the pattern of the Israelite hierarchy, and try to establish the Papal system by an argument drawn from that hierarchy. Moreover, they insist that communion with the Roman See is so necessary that no one can obtain salvation without it. And yet it is not so, by right, that this commonwealth of carnal Israel was so. For the plan of ecclesiastical polity under the Israelite and the Christian dispensation is not the same by divine institution. Nowhere has Christ either instituted that the Church should have a college of Pontiffs and priests, an earthly head, teachers exercising authority, and exercising legislation and jurisdiction, to whom one must obey on account of their title or some succession I know not what; nor has he chosen a certain other seat or place in the world from which the interpretation of his word, or the reason of belief, or laws, or a sure judgment, ought to be sought. Although such things therefore prevail among that people under the Roman Pontiff, they do not prevail by right, and they are not to be ascribed to God but to the Pontiff, who, according to the prophecy of Daniel 7:25, changes times. And yet that people is, that is, because it bears the name of Christ and his word, and "in the midst of it shall be the saints," hoping for the rest, that there are faithful and saints in it (as indeed before the Reformation, in that external communion, there were many saints, afflicted and captive as they were). On account of this hope for the saints, and their external fellowship and mixing, because the kingdom of God was thus in their midst, it was called the Church and People of God. In the same way the Antichrist, though not belonging to the Church but riding the Beast, was to sit in the Church as in the temple of God, and for a time the Church had to be mixed with the Beast in external communion. But because that people, thus subject to the clergy, does not have divine institution, therefore it ascends out of the abyss, deriving the institution of its subjection and all its worship not from God but from men, and even from Satan himself; and therefore it is also going to perdition, since a society and commonwealth of this kind, which does not refer its origins to God as author and founder, remains at last under certain ruin.

units.la: IX. Bestiam talem, quæ fuit, & non est, quamquam est, admiraturi habitantes in terra, quorum nomina non sunt scripta in libro vitæ à fundatione mundi Apoc. xvii. 8. dicuntur. Duo igitur eodem tempore, & in eadem externa communione futura erant hominum genera, puta κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ᾧ θαυμάζονται τὸ θηρίον, habitantium in terra, & admirantium Bestiam; & eorum, quorum γέγραπται τὰ ὀνόματα ἐπὶ τὸ βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου scripta sunt in libro vitæ nomina à fundatione mundi: adeóque reprobi & electi homines Bestiæ, & homines Ecclesiæ in eodem externo coetu. Habitantes in terra & admirati Bestiam sunt, qui vocati & audientes verbum Bestiam, seu Ecclesiam externam qualem descripsimus, in pretio habent, eique humano nomini se subjicienti se se in interna & externa communione adjungunt. Scripti verò in libro vitæ à fundatione mundi, qui in externa communione juncti licet, electi tamen ab æterno, Bestiam; hoc est, Ecclesiam talem in pretio nullo habent, sed potius per illam scandalizantur, & propter abominationes multiplices suspirant.
units.tr: IX. Such a beast, which was, and is not, and yet is, the inhabitants of the earth will marvel, whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world (Rev. 17:8), is spoken of. Two kinds of men, therefore, were to be in the same external communion at the same time: those dwelling on the earth, and admiring the Beast [κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ θαυμάζονται τὸ θηρίον]; and those whose names are written in the book of life from the foundation of the world [γέγραπται τὰ ὀνόματα ἐπὶ τὸ βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου]. Thus there are reprobate men of the Beast and elect men of the Church in the same external assembly. Those dwelling in the earth and admiring the Beast are those who, called and hearing the word, hold the Beast, that is the external Church such as we have described, in high esteem, and who, submitting to that human name, join themselves to it in both internal and external communion. Those written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, who are joined in external communion, yet elect from eternity, hold the Beast, that is such a Church, in no esteem at all, but rather are scandalized by it, and sigh over its manifold abominations.

units.la: X. Talis scilicet erat status Populi illius, qui inde à Pontificia tyrannide in spiritualibus & temporalibus inducta, usque ad separationem, quæ per Reformationem institura est, Ecclesiæ (parentis puta, non dominantis) nomine venit. Erant in externo Ecclesiæ illius gremio duo homi-
units.tr: X. Such, of course, was the state of that people which, from the Papal tyranny introduced in spiritual and temporal affairs, down to the separation that was to be effected by the Reformation, came under the name of the Church (I mean the parent, not the dominant one). In the external bosom of that Church there were two kinds of men.

units.la: Duo genera hominum, Bestiam admirantium, & nullo loco habentium.
units.tr: Two kinds of men: those who admire the Beast, and those who hold it in no regard.

units.la: Eadem genera Imperio Romano Christiano convertuntur. hominum genera, admirantes Bestiam, adeoque homines Bestiæ, & eandem non admirantes, prædestinati ab æterno, homines veræ Ecclesiæ. Illi relicto Dei verbo, humanæ authoritati se subjicientes, ad nutum Cleri dominantis se composuerunt, errantem multitudinem sectati, Papæ, seu supremi in terris Domini seu oracula & jussa universa ἀδιαφόρως receperunt, humanas traditiones, voluntarios cultus, superstitiones varias adoptárunt, denique se non Dei sed Papæ suo quæirentis Spiritu quaquaversum duci flectique passi sunt. Hi vero in externo illo Ecclesiæ corpore, veluti carcere quodam detenti, septique licet ob temporum infelicitatem, infirmitatibus non paucis, per gratiam tamen æternæ prædestinationis, seu scriptionis in libro vitæ, se se pro viribus impollutos à grassantibus abominationibus gesserunt, publica Ecclesiæ in pejus quotidie degenerantis mala deplorárunt, Agni, Cœlestis illius Ducis signa secuti, verbo Dei in præcipuis constanter adhæserunt, veram justitiam & salutis viam extra se in Christo unico salutis & fidei Principe ac Salvatore quæsiverunt, denique ejus rei gratia reliquæ multitudinis, Cleri dominantis maxime ludibria, contumelias, odia, & subinde etiam novissima supplicia alacri animo perpessi sunt, quorum non conteminendam ex quolibet hominum, Imperatorum, Principum, Nobilium, plebejorum genere, nubem, Testium Veritatis Catalogi produnt, & ampliorem etiam dies Domini, qui ad dextram statuet plures, quos ad sinistram in mundo Bestia statuit, manifestabit.
units.tr: The same two kinds of men are applied to the Christian Roman Empire: men who admire the Beast, and so are men of the Beast, and men who do not admire it, predestined from eternity, men of the true Church. The former, having abandoned the word of God and submitting to human authority, conformed to the nod of the dominant clergy, followed the erring multitude, and received without distinction [ἀδιαφόρως] the oracles and all the commands of the Pope, or the supreme Lord on earth; they adopted human traditions, voluntary worship and various superstitions, and in the end allowed themselves to be led and turned this way and that by the spirit of the Pope, not seeking God. But the latter, held in that external body of the Church as in a kind of prison, and hedged in, though by the unhappiness of the times with not a few weaknesses, yet through the grace of eternal predestination, or of being written in the book of life, conducted themselves as far as they could as undefiled by the abominations that raged around them. They lamented the public evils of the Church, which degenerated daily for the worse. Following the signs of the Lamb, that heavenly Leader, they constantly held fast to the word of God in essentials, and they sought true righteousness and the way of salvation outside themselves in Christ, the sole Prince and Saviour of salvation and faith. Finally, for this cause, they bore with cheerful spirit the mockery, insults, hatred of the rest of the multitude, above all of the dominant clergy, and at times even the extreme punishments; of whom the Catalogues of the Witnesses to the Truth reveal a not contemptible cloud, from every class of men: emperors, princes, nobles, commoners; and the day of the Lord, which will set more of them on the right hand, will reveal even more than those whom the Beast sets on the left in the world.

units.la: XI. Habitus externus Bestiæ Apoc. xvii. 3. nomine Coccineo exprimitur. Coccineus Color paludamenti Imperialis color erat. Imperatoris igitur & Imperii Romani, sed servientis jam Mulieri, utpote super Bestiam sedenti status adumbratur. Tum coccineus ille color hieroglyphicum esse potest populi, qui vel per pro-
units.tr: XI. The external appearance of the Beast is expressed by the name scarlet (Rev. 17:3). Scarlet was the colour of the imperial military cloak. The state of the Emperor and the Roman Empire, but now serving the Woman, as she sits upon the Beast, is therefore shadowed forth. Then, that scarlet colour may be a hieroglyph of the people which, either through the profession of faith in Christ, seems coloured with his blood,

units.la: Bestia habitat super septem montes, coccineus, idem Imperii aptatur. sessionem fidei in Christum sanguine ipsius coloratus esse videtur, vel reus etiam est sanguinis coccinei Christi & Sanctorum. Utrumque quomodo populo illi, Clero dominanti subjecto, competat, obscurum nemini esse potest. Externa enim professione nomen dedit Christo per passiones & effusionem sanguinis pro fidelibus consummato, quem ipse Clerus dominans in ore habuit. Vel sola Crucia⁠ tæ militiæ numerosissima cohors, quæ sanguinis Christi in cruce profusi symbolum in corpore gestavit, ejus rei indicium præbet. Tum sanguinis Christi & Sanctorum reus peragitur idem, cùm Christum in sanctis, Pontificiæ factioni reclamantibus, & Christo Domino suo fidem inviolatam præstantibus, nunquam non persecutus est atrociter, cujus rei experimenta non pauca Historia Papatûs repræsentavit, Scriptorésque Ecclesiastici longè plurima commemorant.
units.tr: The Beast dwells upon seven mountains, scarlet; the same is applied to the Empire. or is also guilty of the scarlet blood of Christ and of the saints. How both of these belong to that people, subject to the dominant clergy, can be obscure to no one. For by external profession it gave its name to Christ, who was consummated through sufferings and the shedding of blood for the faithful, and whom the dominant clergy themselves had constantly on their lips. The very numerous cohort of the Crusading army alone, which bore on its body the symbol of the blood of Christ poured out on the cross, gives evidence of this. Then, that it is guilty of the blood of Christ and of the saints is shown by the same thing, since it has always persecuted cruelly Christ in the saints, who opposed the Papist faction and kept their faith inviolate towards Christ their Lord; many instances of this the history of the Papacy has presented, and the ecclesiastical writers record very many more.

units.la: XII. Bestiæ os diductum narratur in blasphemias. Dicitur enim Bestia Coccinea γέμεσα ὀνομάτων βλασφημίας, plena nominibus blasphemiæ. Apoc. xvii. 3. Et ὄνομα nomen quidem in sacris fidei & adorationis objectum, seu id, quod adoratur & in quo fiducia collocatur, non semel denotat. Cui enim confidimus, credimus, paremus, servimus, eum fiduciæ, obsequij, servitutis, spei, omniumque actionum nostrarum authorem ὀνομάζομεν nominamus. Ita Christus exaltatus dicitur ὑπεράνω πάσης ὀνόματος ὀνομαζομένου supra omne nomen quod nominatur. Phil. ii. 9. Et ὁ ὀνομάζων τὸ ὄνομα Χριστοῦ quisquis nominat nomen Domini, abstinere ab iniquitate jubetur. 2 Tim. ii. 19. Neque etiam ὄνομα ἕτερον nomen aliud sub Cælo datum est hominibus in quo oportet nos salvari, quàm Christi Act. iv. 12. Nomen igitur Blasphemiæ seu nomen blasphemum est, cùm in cultu, fide, adoratione, alius quàm Deus, Christus nominatur, aut pro verbo Dei habetur, quod Dei non est, aut cultus adstringitur gitur ad locum certum, quem Deus non elegit, יהוה שם memoriam nominis sui non posuit. Nominatio talis citra nominis Divini, quod alii Deus dare non vult, manifestam detractionem, adeóque iniquissimam blasphemiam contingere nulla potest. Sicut igitur qui cum Agno sunt, dicuntur ὄνομα πατρὸς, αὐτῶ nomen Patris ejus in frontibus gerere, hoc est Patrem colere, adorare, venerari solum Apoc. xiv. 1. dicuntur. Ita Bestia, & qui cum ea sunt nomen ejus, quem colunt, adeóque χάραγμα signaturam Apoc. xiii. 16. in manibus, frontibusque suis gerunt.
units.tr: XII. The mouth of the Beast is said to be opened into blasphemies. For the Scarlet Beast is called full of names of blasphemy [γέμοντα ὀνομάτων βλασφημίας, plena nominibus blasphemiae], Rev. xvii. 3. The word name [ὄνομα] does not once denote only the object of sacred faith and worship, that is, that which is adored and in which trust is placed. For we name [ὀνομάζομεν] the one in whom we trust, believe, obey and serve, the author of all our hope and of all our actions. So Christ exalted is said to be above every name that is named [ὑπεράνω πάσης ὀνόματος ὀνομαζομένου], Phil. ii. 9. And whoever names the name of Christ [ὁ ὀνομάζων τὸ ὄνομα Χριστοῦ] is bidden to depart from iniquity, 2 Tim. ii. 19. Nor is there another name [ὄνομα ἕτερον] given under heaven to men by which we must be saved, other than Christ's, Acts iv. 12. A name of blasphemy, therefore, or a blasphemous name, arises when in worship, faith or adoration someone other than God or Christ is named, or is held to be the word of God when it is not God's, or when worship is tied to a certain place which God has not chosen, where he has not placed the memorial of his name [יהוה שם]. Such naming, without the divine name, which God does not wish to be given to another, cannot happen without manifest detraction and therefore most iniquitous blasphemy. Just as those who are with the Lamb are said to have the name of his Father [ὄνομα πατρὸς αὐτοῦ] written on their foreheads, Rev. xiv. 1, that is, to worship, adore and venerate only the Father, so the Beast and those who are with it bear the name of the one they worship, and so bear the mark [χάραγμα], Rev. xiii. 16, on their hands and foreheads.

units.la: XIII. Populum illum, qui Clero dominanti succubuit, ejusmodi nominibus blasphemiae scatere, manifestum est. Alium enim in cultu suo, quàm solum verum Deum, nominat, Sanctos in Coelo, reliquias, imagines Sanctorum in terra, hostiam in Sacramento, atque in omni re, quæ credenda est, Papam ceu Prophetam, doctorem infallibilem, fidei regulam & principium unicum. Penes nos, qui à Metropoli nostra Romani vocamur, solos, ita populi insaniunt, & Regnum Dei, apud nos Christus est, nos summus Ecclesia Catholica, nostro, aut Metropolcos nostræ nomine fideles omnes vocari debent. Solius Papæ nostri nomen in Ecclesia recitari debet, Romana Ecclesia nostra deficere nequit, æterna, inconcussa erit, quomodo etiam Hieronymus quæst. ii. ad Algas. jactantiam de Roma æterna inter blasphemias refert. Taceo, quòd particeps ille populus est blasphemiarum omnium quas Magistri & Domini ejus adversus nomen Dei, & tabernaculum ejus, & habitantes in Coelo evomunt de quibus in loco uberiús. Non aliam enim fidem, non etiam religionem, quàm ab illis fidei dominantibus jussam, imperatam ampleċtuntur. Denique sicut Romani veteres gentiles blasphemiarum rei habentur merito, eò quòd Romam suam Deam, Imperatores Deos, Divos suos (quos etiam aris, Templis, statuis honorârunt) locum in quo Imperatorum dicta promulgabantur, Theopompium, eò quòd Deorum inibi oracula funderentur, insigniverunt: ita Romani illi Christiani Ecclesiam suam Divinam ob assistentiam immediatam Spiritûs Dei, Pontificem Deum, ejus oracula Divina jactantes, non minùs rei horribilium blasphemiarum sunt.
units.tr: XIII. It is plain that the people who submitted to the dominant Clergy are full of such names of blasphemy. For in their worship they name something other than the one true God: the saints in heaven, relics, images of the saints on earth, the host in the sacrament, and, in every matter that is to be believed, the Pope as prophet, infallible teacher, the sole rule and principle of faith. Among us, who are called Romans after our Metropolis, the peoples rave that the Kingdom of God is with us alone, that Christ is with us, that we are the supreme Catholic Church, and that all the faithful ought to be called by our name or by the name of our Metropolis. Only the name of our Pope ought to be recited in the Church. Our Roman Church cannot fail; it will be eternal and unshaken. So too Jerome, Quaest. ii. ad Algasiam, reports the boast about eternal Rome among the blasphemies. I say nothing of the fact that this people shares in all the blasphemies which their masters and lords vomit against the name of God, his tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven, about which more fully in its place. For they embrace no faith and no religion other than what those who rule in matters of faith command and enjoin. Finally, just as the ancient Roman gentiles are rightly held guilty of blasphemy, because they honoured their Rome as a goddess, their emperors as gods, and their deified ones (whom they also honoured with altars, temples and statues), and named the place where the emperors' sayings were announced Theopompium, because the oracles of the gods were poured forth there, so those Roman Christians, boasting that their Church is divine on account of the immediate assistance of the Spirit of God, and that their Pontiff is God and his oracles divine, are no less guilty of horrible blasphemies.

units.la: XIV. Bestiæ eidem κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ Capita septem, Angelus Mystagogus Apoc. xvii. 3. 9. tribuit, atque mox eadem explicat per ὄρη ἑπτὰ montes septem, quibus ita Romam ἑπτάλοφον sepiticollam indigitari, ut simul etiam statuantur monimenta seu symbola tum septem dynastiarum, Regionum, Provinciarum, quibus universa ditio Romana, ceu sedes propria Mulieris & Bestiæ continetur; tum septem βασιλέων Rectorum, seu Regum Capitaneorum in montibus seu Provinciis illis imperitantium, Differt. iij. 36. abundè demonstravimus.
units.tr: XIV. The Angel, the mystagogue, ascribes to the same Beast seven heads [κεφαλὰς ἑπτά], Rev. xvii. 3, 9, and straightway explains them as seven mountains [ὄρη ἑπτά], by which Rome is pointed out as the seven-hilled city [ἑπτάλοφον]. In this way monuments or emblems are set up at the same time both of the seven dynasties, regions and provinces in which the whole Roman dominion, as the proper seat of the Woman and the Beast, is contained, and of the seven kings, that is, the captain-rulers reigning over those mountains or provinces. We have amply demonstrated this in Dissertation iii. 36.

units.la: XV. Tria heic cognoscere juvat. Primò Romam omnium nò esse ἑπτάλοφον Septicollem, seu septimontiam, quod Differt. j. 38. abundè confirmavimus. De eo qui plura desiderat, Rofinum & Dempsterum Antiquit. R. lib. j. 2. consulat licet. Secundò Romanum Imperium, uti in partes suas divisum semper fuit, ita à Constantino M. nova quadam Provinciarum seu Dynastiarum divisione ita distinctum esse, ut Seculari divisioni illi, etiam Ecclesiastica inhæserit, & ubi Provinciarum plurium corpus aliquod Imperatoris Vicarius rexit, ibidem etiam Ecclesiæ Primus residens Ecclesiam per subjectos Episcopos gubernaverit. Constantinus nempe sub tempus ipsum Nicæni Concilii hunc in Imperio Romano regendarum Provinciarum morem introduxit, ut plures Provincias in unum corpus redactas, uni administrandas dederit. Is Vicarius Præfecti Prætorio, administratio verò ejus διοίκησις Diæcesis vocabatur. Inde nomen plurium Provinciarum numero inditum, quàs illo unus Vicarius sub se habebat. Plures autem Vicarii uni præfecto subeurant, cujus & vices gerebant. Fuerúntque primitùs in toto Imperio Romano constituti Præfecti Prætorio quatuor, additi mox plures. Atque eam divisionem Ecclesia ita secuta est, ut suos quoque Rectores, Patriarchas, Metropolitanos, Episcopos in distinctis Imperii partibus habuerit. Tertiò post Imperium Romanum Constantini operâ ad Christum conversum, non defuisse hypocritas multos, qui in Imperatoris potiùs, quàm Dei & Christi gratiam, Christum Dominum suum confessi sunt, ac de cætero ingenium geniúmque suum animalem, bestialem non exuerunt. Cujus rei testem habemus Eusebium in vita Constantini M. cap. 54. ubi Constantini M. humanitate abusos esse multos, inprimis ἐρωτιαῦ ἀλλὰ τῶν τλὼ ὁκυλησίαν ὑπαδυομένων, ἢ τὸ Χρισιανῶν Φιλαθρώπως κρυμαλιζομένων ὄνομα, fraudulentam simulationem eorum, qui callidè in Ecclesiam irrepebant, & Christianorum nomen falsò, ac speciem tenus præferebant. Additque, insitam Imperatori humanitatem ac bonitatem, & fidei morúmque sinceritatem eò ipsum adduxisse, πισεῶν τῶν χρημάτων τῶν Χριστιανῶν ὡς νομιζομένων, ἵνα τ' ἀληθῆ ἀεὶ αὐτὴ πολασσόμενη ψυχὴ ζωὴν ἀσφαλισμένην, ut crederet fictæ in speciem pietati hominum illorum, qui pro Christianis habebantur, & qui sinceram erga ipsum benevolentiam callida mente simulabant. Quales fuerint plerique illi, statim subortæ hæresec, Christi Domini personam oppugnantes, & hominis arbitrium dignitatémque exaltantes, nec non affectati in Ecclesia gradus, aliáque satis manifestârunt. XVI. Quibus animadversis Prophetiæ applicatio faciet erit. Populus ille magnus, qui Bestiæ nomine venit, non alius quàm Romanus esse potest, quia ejus capita dicuntur montes septem, in quibus Mulier sedet, quæ Romæ Septimontiæ, seu septem montibus insidentis periphrasis est. Neque tamen de illis montibus cuncta dici possunt, quæ de septem montibus Apocalypsis dicit. Montes ergo septem totidem dynastiarum, totidemque Regum, Bestiæ capitum monumentum esse possunt. Scripturam enim per montes, Imperia, partesque Imperii significare Differt. iij. 36. comprobavimus. Simplicissimus proin sensus esse poterit, initio habituram Bestiam, seu magnum illum populum, septem grandes orbis terræ partes, in quibus sedeat, sive totidem gentibus constituram, & in iisdem totidem Reges, qui in montibus, seu Orbis terræ partibus illis Bestiæ sint capita. Habuit autem statim sub Constantino M. suas Romanus populus dynastias, Provinciarum capita, Reges, seu Rectores tum Politicos, puta Vicarios Imperatoris, Prætorio Præfectos, tum Ecclesiasticos, Patriarchas, Primates, cujusmodi esse possunt, v. g. Patriarchæ seu Primates Hierosolymitanus, Alexandrinus, Antiochenus, Constantinopolitanus, Romanus. Habuit quoque Gallia & Hispania suos in Synodis Primates. Atque iisdem etiam in partibus, ceu totidem montibus & dynastiis Præsides & Rectores Politiæ, Imperatoris vicarii & velut Exarchi locum obtinuerunt. Qui septem illi Reges Capitanei, seu Rectores in totidem Imperii partibus non inepte constitui possunt. Tametsi vero sub Constantino M. & post eum iisdem in locis vera Ecclesia fuit, à Patriarchis & Episcopis veris gubernata, negari tamen nequit, hypocritarum magnam colluviem ei permixtam fuisse, quod Eusebium etiam testantem audivimus, atque insuper ita degenerasse populum, ut successu temporis in externo ejus corpore major pars (Sanctorum enim veram Ecclesiam semper excipimus) Babylonis Magnæ Clitellarium veluti jumentum facta fuerit.
units.tr: XV. Three things here are worth knowing. (1) First, that Rome is not the only seven-hilled [ἑπτάλοφος] or seven-mountained city, which we have amply confirmed in Dissertation i. 38. Whoever wants more may consult Rosinus and Dempster, Antiquit. R. lib. i. 2. (2) Secondly, the Roman Empire, which had always been divided into its parts, was from the time of Constantine the Great distinguished by a certain new division of provinces or dynasties, so that the ecclesiastical order adhered to that secular division. Where one Vicar of the Emperor governed a body of several provinces, there the first resident of the Church also governed the Church through subject bishops. Constantine indeed, about the very time of the Council of Nicaea, introduced this custom in the Roman Empire of governing provinces, giving several provinces, brought together into one body, to be administered by one man. He was the Vicar of the Praetorian Prefect, and his administration was called diocese [διοίκησις]. Hence the name was given to the number of provinces which that one Vicar held under him. Several Vicars were subordinate to one Prefect, whose duties they also performed. At first there were four Praetorian Prefects in the whole Roman Empire, and more were soon added. The Church followed this division, so that it also had its own rulers, patriarchs, metropolitans and bishops, in the distinct parts of the Empire. (3) Thirdly, after the Roman Empire had been converted to Christ through the work of Constantine, there were not lacking many hypocrites who confessed Christ their Lord rather for the favour of the Emperor than for the grace of God and of Christ, and who afterwards did not cast off their animal, bestial nature. We have as witness Eusebius, in the Life of Constantine the Great, ch. 54, where he says that many abused the humanity of the Great Constantine, above all the fraudulent pretence of those who craftily crept into the Church and falsely bore, in outward appearance only, the name of Christians. He adds that the Emperor's innate humanity and goodness, and the sincerity of his faith and morals, led him to believe in the feigned piety of those men who were regarded as Christians and who, with cunning minds, pretended a sincere goodwill toward him. What most of those men were like, the heresies that sprang up straightway, attacking the person of Christ the Lord and exalting man's free will and dignity, as well as the ambitious grades sought within the Church, and other things, have made sufficiently plain. XVI. With these things noted, the application of the prophecy will be easy. That great people which comes under the name of the Beast can be none other than the Roman, because its heads are called seven mountains, on which the Woman sits, which is a periphrasis for Rome, the seven-hilled city, or the city sitting on seven hills. Yet not everything that the Apocalypse says of the seven mountains can be said of those mountains. The seven mountains, therefore, can be a monument to as many dynasties and as many kings, the heads of the Beast. For we have shown in Dissertation iii. 36 that in Scripture mountains signify empires and parts of empires. The simplest sense, therefore, will be that at first the Beast, or that great people, would have seven great parts of the world in which it sits, or would be constituted in as many nations, and in these as many kings, who are the heads of the Beast on those mountains, that is, on those parts of the world. Moreover, the Roman people had its dynasties straightway under Constantine the Great, the heads of the provinces, kings or rulers, both political, namely the Emperor's Vicars and Praetorian Prefects, and ecclesiastical, namely patriarchs and primates, such as, for example, the patriarchs or primates of Jerusalem, Alexandria, Antioch, Constantinople and Rome. Gaul and Spain also had their primates in the synods. And in these same parts, as in so many mountains and dynasties, governors and rulers of the state, who held the place of the Emperor's Vicars and, as it were, of exarchs, held office. These seven captain-kings or rulers can not inaptly be appointed in the seven parts of the Empire. Yet although under Constantine the Great, and after him, there was a true Church in those same places, governed by true patriarchs and bishops, it cannot be denied that a great mass of hypocrites was mixed in with it, as we heard even Eusebius testifying, and moreover that the people so degenerated that, in time, the greater part of its outward body (for we always except the true Church of the saints) became like a beast of burden carrying the packsaddle of Babylon the Great.

units.la: XVII. Id ipsum vero Angelus porro testatur, cum v. g. dicit, in Montibus Mulierem sedere, innuens haud dubiè, fore aliquando tempus, ut Mulier Babylonica exorta, septem illos montes occupet, in iisdem regnet, & imperitet. Quod factum eo tempore est, quo Romanus Episcopus à Phoca Imperatore Oecumenicus seu Universalis Episcopus declaratus, adeóque Constantinopolitano etiam, reliquisque Patriarchis & Primatibus universis, ceu illorum dominus Rectórque, prælatus est. Tam sanè Mulier in montibus illis sedit, reliquósque etiam Reges Capitaneos sibi subjugavit, quanquam non diutinum illud in septem montes simul occupatos imperium fuit.
units.tr: XVII. The Angel also bears witness to this same thing when he says, for example, that the woman sits upon the mountains, clearly signalling that a time would come when the Babylonian woman, once she had risen, would occupy those seven mountains, reign over them and rule. This came to pass when the Roman bishop was declared Oecumenical, or Universal, Bishop by the Emperor Phocas, and so was set above the Constantinopolitan Patriarch and all the other Patriarchs and Primates, as their lord and ruler. Certainly the woman sat upon those mountains in this way, and she also subjugated the other kings and captains to herself, although that rule over the seven mountains held together was not lasting.

units.la: XVIII. Quippe οἱ πέντε ἔπεσαν, ὁ εἷς ἐστιν, ὁ ἄλλος οὔπω ἦλθεν, καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ, ὀλίγον αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι, quinque (Reges) ceciderunt, unus est, alius nondum venit, cum venerit, paulisper eum oportet manere, inquit Angelus v. 10. significans, non fore stabilem statum Bestiæ & Meretricis in illis septem montibus, quod eventus ipse abundè probavit. Mox enim non tantùm Persæ magnis incommodis Remp. publicam affecerunt, occupata Mesopotamia & Assyria, in minorem Asiam usque progressi, uti Paulus Diaconus Lib. xvij. Zonaras tomo iij. Beda de ratione temporum, aliíque narrant: Sed etiam Germania, Gallia, Hispania, bonáque Italiæ pars à Phoca defecerunt: Sub Heraclio Phocæ successore Persæ iidem Africam suæ ditionis secerunt, Scythæ Europam lacerarunt, Saraceni Heraclio militantes, cùm stipendiis fraudarentur, maxima multitudine defecerunt, & Mahumede duce per Syriam grassati, Damascum occupárunt, Ægyptum vastárunt, Arabiam subruerunt, Africam universam, & Lybiam ac Hispaniam prope totam subjugárunt: Bulgari Thraciam vastárunt, & Imperii vires non parum attriverunt: Mauritani totis viribus in Hispaniam irruerunt, & suæ illam ditionis secerunt: denique Longobardi Italiam ingressi mirè afflixerunt, atque in ea Regnum erexerunt. Tunc igitur quinque Reges, Vicarii, Prætorio Præfecti, Exarchi Romani Imperatoris, adeoque totidem montes, capita Bestiæ cecederunt, unus erat nempe Græcus seu Constantinopolitanus, ægrè Imperii reliquias illas sustinens, alius nondum venerat, Imperii in Occidente pars, Regnum Italicum, mox tamen erectum, neque stabile illud tamen. Nam cùm venerit, oportet ipsum parumper manere. Neque enim Reges Italici, à Papis adversus Caroli M. filios excitati, diu manserunt, uti ex Sigonii de Regno Italiæ Scriptis libris liquet. Successit enim iis, ceu Regi Septimo, Octavus, seu potestas octava, quæ Romæ imperavit, sed Regnum ipsum extra ditionem Romanam gessit in Germania, cujus Majestatem etiam vicini, cum eodem subinde conspirantes, comiter reverentur. Qui ipse tamen est ex septem, quia est in Italia & Roma, quæ in septem montibus censetur, licet propagines & stolones ultra septem istos montes porrectos habeat. Atque in Octavo-Septimo illo Rege, seu Dynastia, Bestiæ judicium absolvetur. Sequitur enim: Καὶ ὡς ἀπολλύων ἐχθρός, & in interitum vadit.
units.tr: XVIII. Indeed, "five have fallen, one is, the other has not yet come, and when he comes he must remain a little while" [οἱ πέντε ἔπεσαν, ὁ εἷς ἐστιν, ὁ ἄλλος οὔπω ἦλθεν, καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ, ὀλίγον αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι], five (kings) have fallen, one is, the other has not yet come, and when he comes he must remain a little while, says the Angel at v. 10, signifying that the Beast and the Harlot would not have a stable state in those seven mountains, as the event itself has amply proved. For soon not only did the Persians inflict great damage on the commonwealth, occupying Mesopotamia and Assyria and advancing even into Asia Minor, as Paulus Diaconus, Book 17, Zonaras, vol. 3, Bede, De ratione temporum, and others relate; but Germany, Gaul, Spain and a good part of Italy also broke away from Phocas. Under Heraclius, Phocas' successor, the same Persians cut Africa off from his dominion. The Scythians tore Europe apart. The Saracens, serving in Heraclius' army, when they were cheated of their pay, deserted in great numbers and, under Mahomet as leader, overran Syria, occupied Damascus, laid waste Egypt, overthrew Arabia, and subjugated all Africa, Libya and nearly all of Spain. The Bulgarians ravaged Thrace and wore down the strength of the empire not a little. The Mauritanians attacked Spain with all their might and cut it off from his dominion. Finally the Lombards, entering Italy, greatly afflicted it and set up a kingdom there. Then, therefore, five kings, vicars, praetorian prefects and exarchs of the Roman emperor, and so as many mountains and heads of the Beast, fell. One was, namely the Greek or Constantinopolitan, barely sustaining those remnants of the empire. The other had not yet come: the part of the empire in the West, the Italian kingdom, which was soon set up but was not stable. For "when he comes, he must remain a little while." The Italian kings, stirred up by the popes against the sons of Charlemagne, did not last long, as is clear from the books of Sigonius De Regno Italiae. For there succeeded them, as the seventh king, an eighth, or eighth power, which ruled at Rome, but whose kingdom itself lay outside the Roman territory, in Germany, whose majesty even the neighbouring rulers, conspiring with it from time to time, respectfully revere. Yet he himself is among the seven, because he is in Italy and Rome, which is counted among the seven mountains, although he has offshoots and runners stretching beyond those seven mountains. And in that Eighth-Seventh king, or dynasty, the judgment of the Beast will be completed. For it follows: "And he is as an enemy destroying, and goes into destruction" [Καὶ ὡς ἀπολλύων ἐχθρός, & in interitum vadit].

units.la: XIX. Restant Bestiæ cornua. De quibus ita Angelus Apoc. xvii. 12. &c.
units.tr: XIX. The horns of the Beast remain. Of these the Angel speaks thus, Rev. xvii. 12, etc.

units.la: Decem cornua, quæ vidisti, decem Reges sunt, qui Regnum nondum acceperunt, sed potestatem ut Reges unam horam accipiunt cum Bestia. Hi unam sententiam habent, & potentiam & potestatem suam Bestiæ tradent. Hi cum Agno belligerabunt, & Agnus vincet eos, quia Dominus Dominorum est, & Rex Regum &c. Bestiæ capita à cornibus eatenus distingui, quòd illis amputatis Bestiam interire necessum sit, his verò resectis manere eandem nihil prohibeat: singula etiam cornua illa decem non capitibus singulis, sed uni, ultimo scilicet, Octavo-Septimo affigenda esse; Reges illos cum Octavo illo capite non perpetim, sed una hora, hoc est, simul eodem tempore regnaturos, ut Bestiæ patronos, & cum eadem potestatem habentes: denique ita armaturos & defensuros Bestiam, ut ab ea in rebus fidei dissentire liceat nemini; Differt. iij. 39. ostendimus.
units.tr: "The ten horns which you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom, but receive power as kings for one hour together with the Beast. These have one purpose, and they will hand over their power and authority to the Beast. These will make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, because he is Lord of lords and King of kings, etc." The heads of the Beast are distinguished from the horns in this respect: once the heads are cut off the Beast must perish, whereas if the horns are cut away nothing prevents the Beast from remaining the same. Likewise, those ten horns are not to be attached each to a separate head, but to one, namely the last, the Eighth-Seventh; and those kings with that eighth head will reign not continuously but for one hour, that is, at the same time, as patrons of the Beast and having power together with it. Finally, they will so arm and defend the Beast that no one may dissent from it in matters of faith. We showed this in Dissertation III, 39.

units.la: XX. Hæc quemadmodum eventu ipso repræsentata sint, historiæ evidentia ambigere non sinit. Principalis Bestiæ potestas est in Imperatore, cujus sedes est potissimùm Germania. Cum eo alii Reges politicam potestatem habentes sociantur. Ordo igitur & prophetiæ, & historiæ ejusmodi est. Bestia, seu magnus ille populus Romanus, ab initio Capita, Reges Capitaneos, dynastias septem habet, puta, Constantinopolitanam, Hierosolymitanam, Alexandrinam, Antiochenam, Romanam, Gallicam, Hispanicam, quibus singulis, ceu totidem Provinciarum Imperii capitibus plures Provinciæ suberant. Post occupatos à meretrice, seu insessos montes, Capita, Reges illos, sub Phoca Imperatore, mox per irruptiones populorum barbarorum & exoticorum, Persarum, Saracenorum, Bulgarorum; Mauritanorum, Longobardorum cadunt Reges quinque, Hierosolymitanus, Alexandrinus, Antiochenus, Hispanius, Gallus. Unus est, Constantinopolitanus, seu Græcus, Imperator scilicet ipse Orientalis, cum barbaris infeliciter diu satis confligens. Septimus venit, Regnum Italiæ, cui Pontifices ipsi favebunt, & paulisper manet. Postea venit Octavus, cohærens cum reliquis Italiæ Regibus, suo tamen modo novus, Germanus scilicet, auspicia in Othone I. Saxone sortitus. Sed & hunc ipsum oportet in exitium vadere. Antea verò quàm id eveniat, cum Bestia, Populo, qui Romani nomen obtinet, & Meretricem portat, erunt cornua decem, seu totidem præter propter Reges, ex Imperii Romani ruinis exorituri, qui tempore Prophetiæ Regnum nondum acceperunt, sed potestatem ὡς βασιλεῖς ut Reges, puta non pleno jure & absolutè regnantes,
units.tr: XX. How these things have been represented by the event itself, the clarity of history does not allow us to doubt. The principal power of the Beast lies in the Emperor, whose seat is chiefly Germany. With him other kings possessing political power are allied. The order, then, both of the prophecy and of history is as follows. The Beast, that is, the great Roman people, has from the beginning heads, kings as captains, and seven dynasties: namely the Constantinopolitan, Jerusalem, Alexandrian, Antiochene, Roman, Gallic and Spanish, to each of which, as to so many heads of the provinces of the empire, several provinces were subject. After the mountains were occupied and sat upon by the harlot, those heads, those kings, under the Emperor Phocas and soon after through the invasions of barbarian and foreign peoples, the Persians, Saracens, Bulgarians, Mauritanians and Lombards, fall: five kings, the Jerusalemite, Alexandrian, Antiochene, Spanish and Gallic. One is, the Constantinopolitan, or Greek, namely the emperor of the East himself, struggling for a long time, and unsuccessfully, with the barbarians. The seventh comes, the kingdom of Italy, which the popes themselves will favour, and it remains a little while. Afterwards the eighth comes, joined with the remaining kings of Italy, yet new in its own way, namely German, having received its auspices in Otto I, the Saxon. But this one too must go to destruction. Before this happens, however, along with the Beast and the people who bear the name of Rome, and who carry the Harlot, there will be ten horns, or about as many kings, arising from the ruins of the Roman empire, who at the time of the prophecy had not yet received a kingdom, but power as kings, that is, not reigning with full right and absolutely,

units.la: Prophetiæ & complementi ordo. Bestia cornua decem Reges sunt. gnantes, sed vasalli, fiduciárii Papæ, Meretricis Regnum in ipsos Reges terræ obtinentis, unam horam accipientes cum Bestia, hoc est, certo tempore una cum Bestia Octavi mentis, & Regis ejus regnantes, qui unam sententiam habent, & potentiam potestatémque suam Bestiæ tradent, conjungent cum Bestia, & per Bestiam tradent Meretrici super Bestia sedenti, imperanti, in spiritualibus & temporalibus dominanti, quam una cum populo Romano πολεμεῖν & extremis viribus, cum Agno, Christo & Euangelio ejus belligerantes, acerrimè defendent.
units.tr: The order of the prophecy and its fulfilment. The ten horns of the Beast are kings, reigning but as vassals and trustees of the Pope, who holds the kingdom of the Harlot over the kings of the earth, receiving power together with the Beast for one hour, that is, for a certain time, together with the Beast of the eighth head and its king, who have one purpose, and will hand over their power and authority to the Beast: they will join with the Beast and, through the Beast, will hand over to the Harlot sitting upon the Beast, ruling and dominating in spiritual and temporal matters, whom, together with the Roman people, they will defend most fiercely with all their strength, making war [πολεμεῖν] with the Lamb, Christ, and his Gospel.
